title: In-hospital vascular surgery consultation is associated with improved follow-up and earlier identification of aneurysmal degeneration after acute Type A aortic dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Acute Type A aortic dissections (TAAD) are historically managed by cardiac surgery. However, subsequent treatment of residual dissection within the thoracoabdominal aorta often requires vascular surgical intervention and lifelong surveillance. This study assesses long-term outcomes by completeness of follow-up after operative intervention for acute TAAD. METHODS: Patients who underwent surgical intervention for acute TAAD from 2014 to 2025 were identified. Patients who experienced death within 30-days or those with dissection limited to Zone 0/Zone 1 were excluded. Vascular surgery evaluation and time to consultation (index-hospitalization, outpatient, none) was documented. Follow-up was classified as complete, incomplete, or lost (LTF) according to the frequency of contrasted thoracoabdominal imaging, consistent with clinical practice guidelines. Trends in completeness of follow-up were described. Demographics, anatomic/operative characteristics, and perioperative outcomes were compared between complete follow-up and incomplete follow-up/LTF groups. Long-term outcomes (aortic degeneration, planned secondary intervention, survival) were assessed with Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression analysis. RESULTS: 241 patients were included; 80% had vascular surgery consultation (70% inpatient, 30% outpatient) and 86% of consultations occurred within 1-year of index procedure. In total, 46% of patients had complete follow-up, 41% had incomplete follow-up, and 13% were LTF. In-hospital consultation increased by 58% over the study period. Demographics, comorbidities, and anatomic characteristics were similar between groups. Patients with complete follow-up had higher rates of complex arch repair (Zone 1-3) (complete 56% vs. incomplete/LTF 27%, p<0.001), were more likely to undergo genetic testing (complete 52% vs. incomplete/LTF 18%, p<0.001), in-hospital TEVAR extension (7% vs. 2%, p=0.028), and TEVAR extension within 3 months (complete 17% vs. incomplete/LTF 5%, p=0.002). In time-to-event analysis, complete follow-up was associated with more planned secondary interventions (complete: 12% vs. incomplete: 5%, p=0.007) and identified aneurysmal degeneration (32% vs. 15%, p=0.002) within 1-year of acute dissection. Long-term survival differed by completeness of follow-up; 1-year (complete: 97% vs. incomplete: 97% vs. LTF: 91%), 3-years (complete: 92% vs. incomplete: 95% vs. LTF: 81%, p=0.021). There were no aortic-related deaths for patients with complete follow-up and five aortic-related deaths (5%) in patients with incomplete follow-up (p=0.13). In-hospital vascular surgery consultation was associated with complete follow-up (HR 2.87, 95% CI 1.6-5.1) and planned secondary interventions (HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.1-3.9). CONCLUSION: Vascular surgery consultation is associated with increased identification of aneurysmal degeneration, planned secondary interventions, and mid-term survival. These data suggest that longitudinal vascular surgical care, starting with in-hospital consultation, is a critical component of care following acute TAAD and should be strongly considered to ensure appropriate postoperative surveillance and improve long-term patient outcomes.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Acute Type A aortic dissections (TAAD) are historically managed by cardiac surgery. However, subsequent treatment of residual dissection within the thoracoabdominal aorta often requires vascular surgical intervention and lifelong surveillance. This study assesses long-term outcomes by completeness of follow-up after operative intervention for acute TAAD.

title: Optimizing Vessel Preparation in Femoropopliteal Lesions: Does the Chocolate Balloon Deliver on Its Clinical Promise?
abstract: The "leave nothing behind" paradigm using drug-coated balloons (DCBs) has reshaped femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease treatment, though clinical success remains heavily contingent upon optimal vessel preparation. In a recent issue of The American Journal of Cardiology, Li and colleagues address the limitations of conventional plain old balloon angioplasty (POBA) through a propensity score-matched analysis of 508 patients from the multicenter PROMISING registry, comparing specialized vessel preparation using the nitinol-constrained Chocolate balloon against POBA before DCB angioplasty. The Chocolate balloon significantly reduced the primary endpoint of bailout stenting (20.47% vs 29.92%) and facilitated larger final DCB diameters, though these acute mechanical advantages did not translate into statistically significant differences in clinical outcomes at 12 months. This commentary examines this striking "procedural-to-clinical paradox," highlighting how the potent antiproliferative effect of DCBs and the acute compensatory function of bailout stents may temporarily mask early clinical divergence. Given that cumulative mechanical failures of permanent metallic implants typically emerge beyond one year in hostile biomechanical environments, longer-term observation remains essential to capture the true clinical dividend of a stent-free strategy.

The Chocolate balloon significantly reduced the primary endpoint of bailout stenting (20.47% vs 29.92%) and facilitated larger final DCB diameters, though these acute mechanical advantages did not translate into statistically significant differences in clinical outcomes at 12 months.

title: The Moderating Effects of Race and Ethnicity on a Motivational Interviewing Intervention for Improving Physical Health Among Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease: Secondary Analysis of a Pilot Randomized Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In a pilot randomized trial, face-to-face or telephone motivational interviewing (MI) was more efficacious than a smartphone app after 3 months for increasing 6-minute walk distance (primary outcome) and reducing body weight (secondary outcome) in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD). Little is known about intervention heterogeneity related to social determinants of health (SDOH). OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore whether SDOH are associated with the MI intervention effects on walking distance and weight loss and generate intervention heterogeneity hypotheses. METHODS: Community dwellers in Wichita, Kansas, were recruited through community outlets and screened for PAD. Consented participants were randomly assigned to MI (n=16) or an app (n=13). Survey instruments were used to measure SDOH, demographics, and adverse childhood experiences, which were assessed for their associations with 6-minute walk distance change and weight loss. Difference-in-differences (DiD) comparisons of median changes between SDOH strata were conducted using Wilcoxon and Kruskal-Wallis nonparametric tests. RESULTS: For 6-minute walk distance, pretest-posttest changes were significantly greater among participants of "other" race and ethnicity than among non-Hispanic White participants (DiD=44.0 m, 95% CI 19.2-164.2; P=.004), and no DiDs for other SDOH were significant. Significant median pretest-posttest increases in walking distance were observed in those with a college or higher educational attainment (48.8 m, 95% CI 28.0-61.4), unmarried individuals (40.4 m, 95% CI 0.5-56.0), those living with family (55.7 m, 95% CI 30.5-199.5), those who talked to and saw family or friends 3 or more times a week (46.4 m, 95% CI 17.2-69.4), and those without unmet daily needs (46.5 m, 95% CI 7.6-67.1). For weight loss, we did not observe significant DiDs with any SDOH. However, a significant median weight loss was observed in every SDOH stratum where we observed a significant increase in 6-minute walk distance. Significant weight loss was also observed in 5 additional SDOH strata: male individuals, household income below US $30,000, never served in military, employed status, and no stress. The improvements in weight loss and walking distance were highly consistent in both direction and size across SDOH strata. CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study was the first to explore potential SDOH-related intervention effect modification and heterogeneity. The significant association between walking distance and race and ethnicity suggested a potential effect modification. Significant pretest-posttest improvements in both outcomes were found in the same SDOH strata. The highly consistent evidence across both outcomes and all SDOH strata provided confidence in potential intervention efficacy and heterogeneity despite the small sample size. Our findings were consistent with established associations between SDOH and general functions in patients with PAD, suggesting likely mediation pathways through health literacy and social support. Future interventions should consider heterogeneity to target socially disadvantaged patients with PAD to bridge disparities and maximize benefits. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03694652; https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT03694652. INTERNATIONAL REGISTERED REPORT IDENTIFIER (IRRID): RR2-10.2196/30295.

Little is known about intervention heterogeneity related to social determinants of health (SDOH). OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore whether SDOH are associated with the MI intervention effects on walking distance and weight loss and generate intervention heterogeneity hypotheses.

title: Association between elevated lipoprotein (a) and venous thromboembolism: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established cardiovascular risk factor linked to atherogenesis, inflammation, and thrombosis; however, its association with venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain, with inconsistent findings across observational studies. AIMS: To systematically evaluate the association between elevated Lp(a) levels and VTE risk and to examine differences by study design. METHODS: 2 2 PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception through January 2026 for observational studies assessing Lp(a) and VTE. Effect estimates (odds ratios [ORs] or hazard ratios [HRs]) were pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Heterogeneity was assessed using Iand τ. Risk of bias was evaluated with ROBINS-E, publication bias with funnel plots, Egger's and Begg's tests, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. The primary outcome was VTE; secondary outcomes included deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and recurrent VTE. RESULTS: 2 2 2 Eleven studies (6 case-control, 5 cohort; 63,325 participants; 3581 VTE events) were included. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a borderline increased VTE risk (pooled OR/HR 1.34 [95% CI 1.00-1.80]; P = 0.049), with high heterogeneity (I = 77.8%) and a wide prediction interval (0.56-3.21). In stratified analyses, case-control studies showed a significant association (OR 1.88 [1.25-2.81]; I = 57.2%), whereas cohort studies showed no association (HR 0.99 [0.85-1.15]; I = 0%), with significant between-group differences (p < 0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: The association between elevated Lp(a) and VTE appears limited to case-control studies and is not supported by prospective cohort data, suggesting potential bias or residual confounding. Further large-scale and genetic studies are warranted to clarify this relationship.

title: Saint-Bonnet Doppler waveform classification system: a scoping review and evidence-based appraisal using AGREE II and AGREE-REX.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Doppler waveform interpretation is central to the diagnosis and surveillance of lower limb peripheral arterial disease (PAD). Despite widespread clinical use of duplex ultrasound (DUS) and hand-held Doppler (HHD), waveform terminology remains highly variable and non-standardised across institutions. The Saint-Bonnet classification, proposed by the French College of Teachers in Vascular Medicine (CEMV), offers a structured eight-category morphological framework mapped to haemodynamic severity. Its evidence base and methodological quality have never been formally appraised. METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). MEDLINE (Ovid) and Embase (Ovid) were searched from 1946 to November 2025. Studies describing, applying, validating, or evaluating the Saint-Bonnet classification were eligible. Data were extracted using a standardised form. Methodological quality was appraised using AGREE II (six domains) and AGREE-REX (three domains), independently by two reviewers (H.A. and F.A.). RESULTS: κ κ κ Seven studies met the inclusion criteria; all published between 2017 and 2022 from a single French vascular research group. The Saint-Bonnet classification achieved a categorisation rate of 98.2% across 1,033 waveforms, outperforming alternative systems. Inter-rater reliability was moderate ( ≈ 0.55). Waveform grade independently correlated with maximal walking distance, and waveform-guided ankle-brachial index (ABI) selection achieved near-perfect agreement with guideline standards (up to 1.00). Automated neural network classification reached = 0.79, approaching expert agreement. AGREE II appraisal revealed high scores for Clarity of Presentation and Scope & Purpose (97% and 83%), but low scores for Rigour of Development and Applicability (44% and 40%). AGREE-REX demonstrated high Clinical Applicability and Implementability. CONCLUSION: The Saint-Bonnet classification is a promising and practical framework for Doppler waveform interpretation, with consistent findings across the available studies. Low AGREE II scores for Rigour of Development and Applicability reflect gaps in its documented development and reporting rather than evidence against its clinical performance. However, all supporting evidence originates from a single, non-independent French research group, and the classification has not undergone external validation; broader adoption should await independent, multicentre confirmation of these findings.

The Saint-Bonnet classification, proposed by the French College of Teachers in Vascular Medicine (CEMV), offers a structured eight-category morphological framework mapped to haemodynamic severity.

title: Optimization of direct oral anticoagulant prescribing in primary care: a pharmacotherapeutic review in real-world clinical practice and therapeutic efficiency.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Direct oral anticoagulants are among the first-line treatments for stroke prevention in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation and for the treatment and secondary prevention of venous thromboembolism. The increasing use of these agents poses challenges related to prescribing appropriateness, clinical safety. This study aims to evaluate the impact of a primary care pharmacist-led intervention on the appropriateness of DOAC prescribing, pharmacotherapeutic efficiency, and clinical outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective, quasi-experimental before-and-after study was conducted in the healthcare area of Xarxa Santa Tecla (Tarragonès and Baix Penedès, Spain). 791 patients receiving DOAC therapy were included. The intervention comprised multidisciplinary educational activities, individualized pharmacotherapeutic review, and communication of recommendations to prescribers. RESULTS: The mean age was 78.2 years, and 43.2% of patients had moderate or severe renal impairment. The pharmacotherapeutic review identified 527 patients (66.6%) as candidates for treatment optimization, through a proposed switch from apixaban to dabigatran. The pharmacist intervention was associated with changes in prescribing patterns among newly initiated patients, increasing the use of dabigatran. The economic analysis estimated savings of €75,508.81 from new treatment initiations and €31,288.25 from therapeutic switches, resulting in total savings of €106,797.06 in 2025. The overall bleeding rate remained stable (5.3% in 2024% vs. 5.2% in 2025), with no deterioration in clinical safety. In conclusion, a structured, multidisciplinary, and coordinated primary care pharmacist-led intervention promoted a more efficient use of healthcare resources, while no deterioration in population-level safety indicators was observed. These findings reinforce the role of primary care pharmacists in optimizing anticoagulant therapy.

This study aims to evaluate the impact of a primary care pharmacist-led intervention on the appropriateness of DOAC prescribing, pharmacotherapeutic efficiency, and clinical outcomes.

title: Abdominal aortic angiosarcoma following endovascular aneurysm repair: case report and analysis of existing literature.
abstract: Abdominal aortic angiosarcoma following endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) is an exceptionally rare and aggressive malignancy that may mimic common EVAR-related complications. We report the case of a 72-year-old man who presented with progressive lower back pain and was initially suspected of having a graft infection. Imaging revealed a periaortic mass involving a previously treated abdominal aortic aneurysm. Biopsy confirmed aortic angiosarcoma. No regional lymph node or distant metastases were identified. The patient underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy with gemcitabine and docetaxel, followed by radiotherapy and surgical resection of the abdominal aorta and EVAR graft with aortic reconstruction. Histopathological examination demonstrated complete pathological response without evidence of residual angiosarcoma. Our literature review identified only 21 reported cases of abdominal aortic angiosarcoma following EVAR, including the present case, underscoring the exceptional rarity of this entity and the limited evidence available to guide diagnosis and treatment. This case highlights the importance of considering aortic angiosarcoma in patients with persistent symptoms and atypical periaortic findings after EVAR and suggests that early biopsy and a multidisciplinary, multimodal treatment approach may improve outcomes despite the generally poor prognosis associated with this disease.

Imaging revealed a periaortic mass involving a previously treated abdominal aortic aneurysm.

title: Association of red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio with ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Critically ill patients with aortic dissection remain at high risk of adverse ICU outcomes, including ICU mortality. The red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) has been investigated as a prognostic marker in various clinical settings. This study aimed to evaluate the association of RAR with ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection. METHODS: Data were extracted from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database. ICU mortality was defined as the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included sepsis during hospitalization/ICU stay, acute kidney injury (AKI), and renal replacement therapy (RRT) use. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to assess the discriminative performance of RAR for ICU mortality. The optimal RAR cutoff was determined using Youden's index and was considered exploratory. Calibration plots and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate model performance. RESULTS: P P P RAR showed modest discrimination for ICU mortality (AUC: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.552-0.765). The exploratory cutoff value of RAR was 5.182. Compared with the low-RAR group, the high-RAR group had higher ICU mortality (21.8% vs. 6.7%; < 0.001), a higher prevalence of sepsis during hospitalization/ICU stay (82.8% vs. 61.1%; < 0.001), and more frequent RRT use (33.3% vs. 9.4%; < 0.001). The AUC increased from 0.706 for SOFA alone to 0.731 for SOFA plus RAR, indicating only limited incremental discrimination. CONCLUSION: Higher early-ICU RAR was associated with ICU mortality and other adverse ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection, but its discrimination was modest, its incremental value beyond SOFA was limited, and external validation is required.

The red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) has been investigated as a prognostic marker in various clinical settings. This study aimed to evaluate the association of RAR with ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection.

title: Peripheral vascular trauma in a civilian Asian trauma centre: Epidemiology, management and outcomes over 9 years.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral vascular injuries (PVI) are uncommon but potentially limb-threatening complications of extremity trauma. Most existing literature originates from military settings or Western trauma systems. We aimed to describe the epidemiology, management strategies, and outcomes of traumatic PVI in a civilian tertiary trauma centre in Singapore. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the institutional trauma registry of Tan Tock Seng Hospital between January 2013 and December 2021. Patients presenting with upper or lower extremity vascular injuries were identified using Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) coding. Demographics, injury characteristics, anatomical injury patterns, interventions, and outcomes including limb salvage, complications, and inpatient mortality were analysed. Comparisons between upper and lower limb injuries were performed using appropriate statistical tests. RESULTS: Among 77,990 trauma admissions, 180 patients sustained PVI (incidence 0.23%). Median age was 36 years and 87% were male. Overall, penetrating trauma was more common (58.9%), but lower limb injuries were predominantly due to blunt trauma (68%), particularly road traffic accidents. Lower limb PVIs were associated with higher injury severity than upper limb PVIs (p < 0.001). Operative management was required in most arterial and venous injuries. Primary repair and endovascular interventions demonstrated excellent limb salvage, whereas bypass procedures were associated with lower salvage rates. Overall limb salvage for lower limb PVI was 88%, with an amputation rate of 10% and mortality of 3%. Most (93%) were functionally independent at discharge. CONCLUSIONS: PVI predominantly affects young male patients and are commonly associated with blunt trauma from road traffic accidents. Despite significant injury severity, favourable limb salvage and functional outcomes can be achieved with timely multidisciplinary management. These findings highlight the importance of coordinated multidisciplinary trauma care in optimizing outcomes following extremity vascular trauma.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Peripheral vascular injuries (PVI) are uncommon but potentially limb-threatening complications of extremity trauma. Most existing literature originates from military settings or Western trauma systems. We aimed to describe the epidemiology, management strategies, and outcomes of traumatic PVI in a civilian tertiary trauma centre in Singapore.

title: Prevalence of Guideline-Recommended Genetic Testing in Patients at Risk for Heritable Thoracic Aortic Disease.
abstract: Heritable thoracic aortic diseases (HTAD) include genetic conditions that increase risk of thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection. The 2022 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) guidelines recommend genetic testing for at-risk individuals, but real-world uptake remains unclear. We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts. We conducted a retrospective study using the TriNetX Research Network (2005-2025). Three guideline-based cohorts were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes: (1) thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, (2) family history of thoracic aortic disease, and (3) nonthoracic arterial aneurysms. Genetic testing was defined by ICD-10-CM codes for genetic screening or susceptibility. Testing prevalence was stratified by age, sex, race, and ethnicity, and annual testing incidence (2005-2024) was evaluated. Among 57,935 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, 1,205 (2.09%) underwent genetic testing. Among 2,811,862 patients with a family history of thoracic aortic disease, 66,699 (2.38%) received testing. Among 347,000 patients with nonthoracic arterial aneurysms, 4,913 (1.42%) underwent testing. Testing was consistently higher in females than males and varied across age groups. Annual testing incidence increased over time but remained <0.6% by 2024. In conclusion, genetic testing for HTAD remains markedly underutilized, with <2.5% of at-risk patients tested despite guideline recommendations, highlighting persistent implementation gaps and the need to improve equitable access to genetic evaluation.

The 2022 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) guidelines recommend genetic testing for at-risk individuals, but real-world uptake remains unclear. We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts.

title: From recanalization to recovery: inflammation and futile reperfusion after mechanical thrombectomy.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has markedly improved reperfusion outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion. However, successful angiographic reperfusion does not invariably translate into functional independence. Poor functional outcome despite successful angiographic reperfusion is commonly described as futile reperfusion. This clinical-angiographic mismatch may reflect persistent tissue injury, including inflammatory injury, alongside pretreatment damage and other determinants of outcome. Experimental findings and clinical associations implicate persistent inflammatory activation, thrombo-inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, microvascular no-reflow, and blood-brain barrier disruption as contributors to secondary tissue injury after MT. Here, we examine potential inflammatory contributions to futile reperfusion and consider how inflammatory biomarkers might inform risk stratification after MT. Ischemia activates microglia, endothelial cells, platelets, complement pathways, and circulating immune cells. Subsequent reperfusion may amplify oxidative stress, cytokine signaling, neutrophil-endothelial interactions, neutrophil extracellular trap formation, matrix metalloproteinase activity, and barrier failure. Together, these processes can promote microvascular obstruction, cerebral edema, hemorrhagic transformation, infarct growth, and impaired neurological recovery despite successful angiographic reperfusion. Among circulating biomarkers, the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio has been studied repeatedly, alongside platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammation response index, interleukin-6, matrix metalloproteinase-9, and other molecular markers. Their specificity, incremental predictive value, and clinical utility require further validation in standardized thrombectomy cohorts. We therefore view inflammation as a plausible biological link between macrovascular reperfusion and persistent tissue-level injury after MT. From a translational perspective, the immediate priorities are to standardize sampling protocols, characterize dynamic inflammatory trajectories, develop multimodal prediction models, and test biomarker-guided therapeutic strategies.
englishSummary: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has markedly improved reperfusion outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion. However, successful angiographic reperfusion does not invariably translate into functional independence. Poor functional outcome despite successful angiographic reperfusion is commonly described as futile reperfusion.

title: Machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with venous thromboembolism and acute kidney injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypoalbuminemia is a prevalent and critical complication among intensive care unit (ICU) patients with venous thromboembolism (VTE) and acute kidney injury (AKI), significantly associated with increased mortality and prolonged hospitalization. However, reliable tools for early prediction of hypoalbuminemia in this high-risk population remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with coexisting VTE and AKI. METHODS: n n In this retrospective study, data from 585 ICU patients with VTE and AKI were analyzed. Patients were divided into a training cohort ( = 409) and a validation cohort ( = 176). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with standardization was applied for feature selection. Five machine learning models-logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), and support vector machine (SVM)-were developed and evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Decision curve analysis (DCA), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and feature importance were performed for the optimal model. The performance of the best machine learning model was compared with conventional ICU severity scores (APSIII, LODs, and OASIS). RESULTS: The standardized LASSO regression identified ten optimal predictors: creatinine (cr), age, tumor/cancer, body mass index (BMI), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), urine output, D-dimer (D_D), Charlson comorbidity index, anticoagulant use, and alanine aminotransferase (ALT). Among the five models, XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance with a validation AUC of 0.882 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.832-0.924], followed by RF (AUC = 0.878), LightGBM (AUC = 0.870), LR (AUC = 0.838), and SVM (AUC = 0.662). The 5-fold cross-validation AUC for XGBoost was 0.901 ± 0.042, with minimal overfitting (CV-test difference = -0.019). Decision curve analysis demonstrated favorable clinical net benefit of the XGBoost model across a wide range of threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis and feature importance consistently identified urine output, age, LDL, BMI, and D-dimer as the top contributors. Compared with conventional ICU severity scores, the XGBoost model significantly outperformed APSIII (AUC = 0.661), LODs (AUC = 0.652), and OASIS (AUC = 0.647). The logistic regression-based nomogram achieved a C-index of 0.838, providing a user-friendly bedside tool for clinicians. CONCLUSION: The machine learning-based XGBoost model, incorporating ten readily available clinical variables, demonstrated excellent predictive performance for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with VTE and AKI. This model offers a practical and interpretable tool for early risk stratification and may guide proactive nutritional and therapeutic interventions in this vulnerable population.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Hypoalbuminemia is a prevalent and critical complication among intensive care unit (ICU) patients with venous thromboembolism (VTE) and acute kidney injury (AKI), significantly associated with increased mortality and prolonged hospitalization. However, reliable tools for early prediction of hypoalbuminemia in this high-risk population remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with coexisting VTE and AKI.

title: Factors associated with mortality in patients with atrial fibrillation: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study synthesized published meta-analyses to assess the quality, bias, and strength of evidence regarding mortality risk factors in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). METHODS: Web of Science, Embase, PubMed, and Cochrane database were used to search the literature up to May 2025. Eligible studies were systematic reviews or meta-analyses investigating AF-related mortality risk factors. AMSTAR tool was used to assess methodological quality and GRADE was used to evaluate evidence certainty. RESULTS: A total of 216 risk factors were identified. Among them, 86 showed significant associations with mortality, while 130 did not. Based on GRADE ratings, 11 were high-quality significant factors, and 9 were of moderate-quality. Factors linked to increased mortality included certain medications (digoxin, dronedarone, sotalol; warfarin/VKA vs. NOAC was associated with higher mortality), comorbidities (cancer, COPD, diabetes, anemia, frailty, LVH, peripheral artery disease), demographic characteristics (older age, smoking, BMI <18.5, Latin American ethnicity), and AF subtype (persistent or non-paroxysmal). In contrast, reduced mortality was associated with NOAC or DOAC use, higher BMI (25-30 or ≥30), surgical interventions (catheter ablation, LAAC/LAAO), other medications (SGLT2 inhibitors, statins), and early rhythm control. CONCLUSION: Systematic Review Registration: This review highlights key factors associated with mortality in AF. Increased risk was observed with warfarin/VKA use (vs. NOAC), certain antiarrhythmic drugs, comorbidities, low BMI, older age, smoking, and non-paroxysmal AF. title: Deep Learning-Based Versus Threshold-Based Bone Removal for CT Angiography of Head and Neck Arteriovenous Fistulas: A Retrospective Comparison of Image Quality, Key-Structure Display, and Post-Processing Time.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p p p p Bone overlap at the skull base limits CT angiography (CTA) in head and neck arteriovenous fistulas (hAVFs), and threshold-based bone removal fails where bone and contrast attenuation overlap. Whether deep learning-based removal improves the display of the structures that determine endovascular planning is unknown in a DSA-confirmed cohort. We therefore compared the two methods within the same CTA datasets.In this single-centre retrospective study, 35 patients with DSA-confirmed hAVF underwent head and neck CTA and digital subtraction angiography (DSA) within two weeks of each other, and each CTA dataset was post-processed with both methods on one workstation. Two blinded readers scored the fistula site, feeding artery and draining vein (0 to 2 each) and overall image quality (5-point scale). Scores were compared with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, vessel edge sharpness and post-processing time with paired t tests, and technical visualisation with McNemar's test.Deep learning-based removal displayed the fistula site, feeding artery and draining vein more completely (median total anatomical score 6.00 versus 3.00;< 0.001 for both readers) and overall image quality was higher (5.00 versus 4.00;< 0.001). Objective vessel edge sharpness was concordant (316.47 ± 46.68 versus 273.70 ± 45.66 HU/mm;< 0.001). Technical visualisation was numerically higher (97.1% versus 88.6%) but not significantly so (= 0.248; three discordant pairs), which makes this endpoint inconclusive rather than negative. Post-processing time was shorter (40.56 ± 1.61 s versus 101.70 ± 4.39 s; mean paired difference 61.14 s, 95% CI 59.53 to 62.74 s; paired t test,< 0.001).In DSA-confirmed hAVF, deep learning-based bone removal displayed the structures that determine endovascular planning more completely than threshold-based removal and was about one minute faster per case. It does not replace DSA for definitive assessment of fistula architecture, and the apparent advantage at the cavernous sinus is exploratory and requires external validation in larger multicentre cohorts.

title: Association Between Breast Arterial Calcification on Mammography and Carotid Artery Stenosis on CT Angiography: A Retrospective Study in a Selected Cohort of Women Aged 60-65 Years.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p p Breast arterial calcification (BAC) is an incidental mammographic finding that may be associated with systemic vascular disease. We investigated the association between mammographic BAC and carotid artery stenosis on cervical computed tomography angiography (CTA) in a clinically selected cohort of postmenopausal women aged 60-65 years.This retrospective, single-center study screened 3421 women aged 60-65 years who underwent both mammography and cervical CTA between November 2021 and May 2025. CTA examinations requested from the emergency department or cardiology clinics, examinations not performed within the same calendar year, and prespecified clinical exclusions were removed, leaving 180 women who underwent outpatient CTA for nonspecific symptoms. The median interval between examinations was 131 days. BAC was graded on a 0-3 scale, and carotid stenosis was assessed according to the North American Symptomatic Carotid Endarterectomy Trial (NASCET) criteria, using the greater degree of stenosis on either side as the patient-level value. BAC was analyzed as an ordinal variable, as a categorical variable, and using binary definitions of presence and severity. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, diabetes mellitus, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, and smoking.Clinically significant stenosis (≥50%) was present in 44 women (24.4%). Its prevalence increased from 5.4% in BAC grade 0 to 75.0% in grade 3 (for trend < 0.001). Each one-grade increase in BAC was associated with clinically significant stenosis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 4.23; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.50-8.03;< 0.001). The corresponding aORs were 16.70 (95% CI, 4.99-73.27) for any BAC and 18.49 (95% CI, 5.93-70.46) for BAC grade ≥2. Adding BAC to the clinical model increased the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) from 0.90 to 0.96 (DeLong= 0.005); the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.95. Inter-reader agreement for BAC grading was substantial (weighted κ = 0.79).In this selected cohort of women aged 60-65 years who underwent clinically indicated CTA, BAC was associated with carotid artery stenosis independently of conventional cardiovascular risk factors. These findings do not establish BAC as a screening or prediction tool and require prospective, population-based validation.

title: Development and internal validation of a clinical prediction model for postoperative venous thromboembolism after neurosurgical intervention in patients with traumatic brain injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a critical complication after traumatic brain injury (TBI) surgery. Conventional risk assessment tools were not developed for neurosurgical trauma populations, limiting their applicability. OBJECTIVE: To develop and internally validate an interpretable clinical prediction model for postoperative VTE in TBI surgery patients. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled 1,450 TBI patients who underwent surgery (2016-2024). Seven predictors were selected using Recursive Feature Elimination. Six machine learning algorithms were compared, with logistic regression (LR) selected as the final model. Performance was evaluated using AUC-ROC, calibration, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: Among 1,450 patients, 205 (14.1%) developed postoperative VTE. The LR model achieved AUC-ROC of 0.868 (95% CI: 0.815-0.920) with good calibration (Brier score: 0.085). Seven predictors were identified: age, Barthel index, ASA classification, multiple surgeries, general anesthesia, limb AIS score, and serum magnesium. Compared with Caprini score (AUC: 0.686), the model showed improved discrimination (ΔAUC = 0.182; NRI: 0.559). CONCLUSION: An interpretable model based on seven routinely available variables demonstrated promising performance for postoperative VTE risk stratification in TBI surgery patients. A nomogram and web-based calculator are provided for clinical use.

title: A clinical-deep learning model for prolonged length of stay following endovascular aortic repair.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prolonged length of stay (PLOS) after endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) for abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is associated with increased complications, resource burden, and patient distress. Early identification of high-risk patients remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a predictive model integrating clinical variables and three-dimensional deep learning (3D-DL) features from preoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA) to predict PLOS after EVAR. METHODS: A total of 788 patients with AAA who underwent elective EVAR were enrolled from two hospitals. The internal training cohort consisted of 556 patients, and the external validation cohort included 232 patients. PLOS was defined as a LOS above the 75th percentile of the distribution. A clinical nomogram was developed using LASSO regression followed by multivariate logistic regression. Deep learning (DL) features were extracted from manually segmented computed tomography angiography (CTA) images using a 3D ResNet200 network, and LASSO regression was applied to select the most informative features. An ensemble model integrating the clinical predictors and the selected DL features was constructed. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: LASSO combined with multivariate logistic regression identified five independent clinical predictors: age, hemoglobin, albumin, maximum aneurysm diameter, and diabetes. The clinical model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.917 in the internal cohort and 0.944 in the external cohort. From the 3D ResNet200 network, 32 DL features were extracted. LASSO regression further selected two of these features. The ensemble predictive model, which integrated the clinical predictors and DL features, demonstrated improved discrimination, with an AUC of 0.971 in the internal cohort and 0.958 in the external cohort. Internal validation with 1,000 bootstrap resamples yielded optimism-corrected AUCs of 0.911 for the clinical model and 0.966 for the ensemble model. Subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent model performance across age and diabetes strata, while performance in the female subgroup warrants further evaluation in larger cohorts. CONCLUSION: This study developed an ensemble predictive model to predict PLOS following EVAR. The model demonstrated excellent discrimination and provided significant prognostic value beyond clinical variables alone. This nomogram may serve as a preoperative tool for risk stratification and resource planning in this population. Future studies should focus on prospective validation and clinical integration.

title: Lipoprotein(a) and Triglycerides as Independent Predictors of Long-Term Aortoiliac Stent Failure After Endovascular Revascularisation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Restenosis and occlusion remain important after aortoiliac stenting, and device choice does not fully explain late patency loss. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is implicated in atherosclerotic progression and residual vascular risk. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether baseline Lp(a) is associated with long-term restenosis or occlusion after aortoiliac stenting. METHODS: This post hoc biomarker analysis of COBEST included 125 patients and 168 treated iliac arteries randomised to the Advanta V12 covered stent (Atrium Medical Corporation, Hudson, NH, USA) or bare-metal stents for symptomatic aortoiliac occlusive disease. The primary outcome was loss of primary patency, defined as restenosis or occlusion during 5-year follow-up. Cox proportional hazards modelling and cumulative failure curves were the main analyses. RESULTS: p p p p In the Lp(a)-adjusted Cox model, covered stent use was associated with a lower hazard of restenosis or occlusion (HR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.31-0.97;= 0.039), whereas each 1 mg/dL higher Lp(a) concentration was associated with a higher hazard (HR, 1.08; 95% CI, 1.06-1.10;< 0.001; equivalent to HR, 2.16; 95% CI, 1.79-2.59 per 10 mg/dL increase). In the biomarker-adjusted model, each 1 mg/dL higher Lp(a) concentration (HR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.02-1.08;< 0.001; HR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.22-2.16 per 10 mg/dL increase) and each 1 mmol/L higher triglyceride concentration (HR, 1.89; 95% CI, 1.34-2.68;< 0.001) remained associated with restenosis or occlusion. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) and, to a lesser extent, triglycerides were independently associated with long-term aortoiliac stent failure after adjustment for stent type.

title: Retinal Microvascular Abnormalities, White Matter Injury, and Cognitive Impairment in Carotid Stenosis or Occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe carotid artery stenosis or occlusion (CASO) is associated with white matter injury and cognitive impairment, but markers of accompanying microvascular dysfunction remain incompletely characterized. We investigated the relationships among retinal microvascular abnormalities on optical coherence tomography angiography, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), and cognitive impairment in severe unilateral CASO. METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 860 participants were included: 566 patients with severe unilateral CASO without acute cerebral infarction and 294 control participants with similar age and sex distributions. All participants underwent multimodal imaging, including automated WMH segmentation on brain magnetic resonance imaging and macular optical coherence tomography angiography. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. RESULTS: P Compared with controls, patients with CASO showed lower vessel length density across retinal layers and greater WMH burden. Within the group with CASO, the retina ipsilateral to the stenosis showed lower vessel length density and greater vessel dilation, paralleling the greater burden of deep WMH in the ipsilateral hemisphere (all adjusted<0.05). Retinal microvascular abnormalities and greater WMH burden were both associated with worse concurrent cognitive performance. Adding optical coherence tomography angiography metrics to clinical and WMH-based models provided modest additional discrimination for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment in internal cross-validation, increasing the area under the curve from 0.652 to 0.695 (Δarea under the curve, 0.043 [95% CI, 0.021-0.064]). CONCLUSIONS: In severe unilateral CASO, retinal microvascular abnormalities were associated with ipsilateral white matter injury and lower cognitive performance. Optical coherence tomography angiographymetrics provided modest complementary discriminatory information beyond conventional clinical variables and WMH for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment, although external validation is required. title: Advances in Design and Preparation of Biodegradable Inferior Vena Cava Filters.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with pulmonary embolism (PE) constituting its most fatal clinical consequence. Inferior vena cava filters (IVCFs) have been employed as a mechanical prophylactic strategy for patients with contraindications to anticoagulation or recurrent embolic events. However, permanent implantation and limited retrieval success are associated with device-related complications, including caval perforation, migration, fracture, and filter-induced thrombosis. Biodegradable IVCFs have been investigated as an alternative approach to provide temporary protection while avoiding the complications associated with long-term implantation. This review discusses recent advances in biodegradable IVCFs from a material perspective, focusing on material selection, structural design, degradation characteristics, and biological responses. Biodegradable polymers, degradable metallic materials, and shape-memory systems are evaluated regarding their mechanical stability, degradation behavior, vascular compatibility, and functional requirements. Strategies for improving radiopacity while preserving biodegradability are also summarized. Despite ongoing progress, key challenges remain in precisely controlling degradation kinetics, maintaining adequate mechanical support during the therapeutic period, and validating long-term safety through clinical studies. Further efforts in material optimization, biofunctional modification, and individualized fabrication may facilitate the future development of biodegradable IVCFs.

title: Redox Dysregulation in the Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Wall: Ferroptosis and Experimental Therapeutic Opportunities.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a spatially heterogeneous disease of the aortic wall for which no pharmacological treatment has reliably arrested enlargement. The term oxidative stress encompasses processes that differ in chemical form, anatomical location and cellular effect. This narrative review examines haem and redox-active iron, phospholipid peroxidation and antioxidant defence at the intraluminal thrombus-wall interface and within medial and inflammatory cells. We distinguish ferroptosis from redox effects on coagulation, migration and secretion and relate these functions to wall remodelling. Experimental studies show that manipulating iron uptake and ferritin turnover, membrane phospholipid susceptibility or peroxide detoxification can alter vascular smooth muscle cell survival, macrophage behaviour and aortic injury. The cellular function affected helps determine which process an intervention should preserve or suppress. Based on evidence from human tissue and animal models, we review opportunities to localise, manipulate and monitor these processes and assess their relevance to established AAA. Testing after confirmation of aneurysm formation, with target engagement in defined wall cells and parallel assessment of systemic effects, is needed to determine whether these approaches can limit continued enlargement.

title: Functional Benefit and Safety of Adjunctive Intra-Arterial Thrombolysis After Successful Endovascular Thrombectomy: An Updated and Cumulative Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: 2 p Adjunctive intra-arterial thrombolysis (IAT) after successful endovascular thrombectomy has been associated with a higher probability of excellent functional recovery in previous randomized-trial meta-analyses. Since those syntheses, the evidence base has expanded to include IAT-TOP, restricted to basilar artery occlusion, and CHOICE-2, in which 90-day mortality was 12.1% with adjunctive alteplase and 6.4% with thrombectomy alone. We therefore examined how the efficacy and mortality profiles changed as randomized evidence accumulated.This PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251006577). Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing adjunctive intra-arterial fibrinolytic therapy administered after trial-defined successful or near-successful post-thrombectomy reperfusion with no adjunctive intra-arterial fibrinolysis. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched through 15 August 2026, with ClinicalTrials.gov searched separately. Nine RCTs comprising 2828 randomized participants were included at the systematic-review level. Event counts were re-extracted from primary trial publications and pooled as risk ratios (RRs) using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals (CIs). Cumulative meta-analysis tracked how the efficacy and mortality estimates changed as evidence accumulated, while fragility analyses assessed the stability of the corresponding statistical inferences. This research received no external funding.Adjunctive IAT increased excellent functional recovery (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-1; 8 RCTs; RR 1.266, 95% CI 1.135-1.412; I= 0.0%), with a 95% prediction interval of 1.047-1.530 and a meta-analytic Fragility Index of 15. Ninety-day all-cause mortality did not differ significantly between groups (8 RCTs; RR 1.036, 95% CI 0.817-1.314); immediately before CHOICE-2 entered the cumulative synthesis, the corresponding estimate was RR 0.984 (95% CI 0.801-1.209). In the bidirectional reverse-fragility analysis, the earliest significance transition identified by the search occurred after 24 one-patient event-status modifications and was in the direction of increased mortality with adjunctive IAT (RR 1.174, 95% CI 1.002-1.377;= 0.048). No transition toward reduced mortality was identified through the same modification depth. No trial was judged to be at high risk of bias using RoB 2. GRADE certainty was moderate for excellent functional recovery, 90-day mortality, and functional independence and low for hemorrhagic outcomes.The efficacy and mortality components of the benefit-risk profile of adjunctive IAT have not evolved in parallel. The improvement in excellent functional recovery persisted as randomized evidence accumulated and remained comparatively stable to perturbation of the observed event data, whereas mortality remains unresolved. The cumulative and reverse-fragility findings do not establish a treatment-related mortality excess; however, the absence of statistical significance should not be interpreted as affirmative evidence of mortality neutrality. The current randomized evidence therefore supports a reproducible functional benefit while preserving clinically relevant uncertainty regarding survival.

title: Temporal changes in dilated ascending aorta after transfemoral TAVR: a comparative analysis of bicuspid and tricuspid aortic valves.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) addresses valvular obstruction but leaves concomitant ascending aortic dilatation untreated. Whether bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) morphology inherently accelerates post-TAVR aortic expansion compared with tricuspid aortic valves (TAV) remains uncertain. METHODS: n n This retrospective cohort study included 189 older adults (BAV, = 87; TAV, = 102) with severe aortic stenosis and ascending aortic dilatation (≥4.5 cm) undergoing TAVR. Annualized aortic expansion rates were evaluated utilizing linear mixed-effects models derived from serial computed tomography angiography over a median 27.0-month follow-up. RESULTS: P P No ascending aortic dissection, rupture, or elective aortic interventions occurred during follow-up. The adjusted annualized expansion rate at the mid-ascending aorta was low and comparable between the BAV and TAV cohorts (0.43 vs. 0.39 mm/year; interaction = 0.364). Progression rates at the distal ascending aorta and sinuses of Valsalva similarly demonstrated no significant morphological differences. No patient exhibited rapid progression (>5 mm/year). Although moderate or greater paravalvular leakage occurred exclusively in BAV patients (4.8% vs. 0.0%; = 0.043), its overall incidence was low (2.2%); however, the extremely small number of cases precluded a definitive statistical assessment of its impact on longitudinal aortic expansion. CONCLUSIONS: In this selected cohort, dilated ascending aortas exhibited slow intermediate-term expansion following transfemoral TAVR utilizing self-expanding valves, with comparable rates between BAV and TAV morphologies. These findings suggest that conservative management of concomitant ascending aortic dilatation may be a reasonable strategy in older TAVR candidates during intermediate-term follow-up, provided that strict blood pressure control and rigorous imaging surveillance are maintained.

Whether bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) morphology inherently accelerates post-TAVR aortic expansion compared with tricuspid aortic valves (TAV) remains uncertain. METHODS: n n This retrospective cohort study included 189 older adults (BAV, = 87; TAV, = 102) with severe aortic stenosis and ascending aortic dilatation (≥4.5 cm) undergoing TAVR.

title: Sitting Baduanjin-based rehabilitation programme following endovascular therapy in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia: protocol for a WeChat mini program-assisted multicentre randomized controlled trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular therapy (EVT) is an important revascularization strategy for limb salvage in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). However, despite restoration of blood flow, patients may continue to experience residual haemodynamic impairment and ischaemia-related burden after EVT, with a persistently high risk of adverse limb outcomes. Therefore, effective post-EVT rehabilitation strategies are needed to further improve limb perfusion and promote functional recovery and symptom improvement in this population. Exercise rehabilitation is widely recommended for patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), but current evidence is largely derived from individuals with intermittent claudication, and its applicability and additional benefits in patients with CLTI after EVT remain uncertain. Sitting Baduanjin (SBDJ) is a low-intensity mind-body exercise modality that reduces lower-limb loading and postural demands while providing exercise stimulation, with potential cardiovascular regulatory effects, and may therefore be suitable for patients with limited exercise tolerance after EVT. However, evidence regarding the effects of SBDJ on target-limb haemodynamic status and patient-centred outcomes in patients with CLTI following EVT remains limited. METHODS: This prospective, multicentre, parallel-group randomised controlled trial incorporates blinded outcome assessment. A total of 146 eligible patients with CLTI following EVT will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention group or the control group. The intervention group will receive SBDJ combined with ankle pump exercise, whereas the control group will receive ankle pump exercise. A WeChat mini program will support exercise delivery, adherence monitoring, follow-up management, and questionnaire data collection during the home-based phase. The primary outcome is the longitudinal change in target-limb ABI over the 12-week rehabilitation period. Secondary outcomes include walking ability, quality of life, anxiety symptoms, lower-limb rest pain, and safety. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, week 4, and week 12. DISCUSSION: Clinical Trial Registration: This trial aims to determine whether an SBDJ-based rehabilitation programme provides additional benefits over ankle pump exercise alone on index-limb haemodynamic status among patients with CLTI following EVT, while exploring its potential effects on functional outcomes and patient-reported outcomes during the early post-EVT rehabilitation period.http://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/, identifier: ITMCTR ITMCTR2022000113.

title: Periprocedural body temperature and clinical outcomes after successful reperfusion in large vessel occlusion stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Functional recovery remains heterogeneous among patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke, even after successful reperfusion. Body temperature may constitute a potentially modifiable physiological factor associated with functional outcome. In particular, whether clinical factors, including baseline stroke severity, modify this temperature-outcome association remains uncertain. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 219 patients with large-vessel occlusion acute ischemic stroke (LVO-AIS) who underwent EVT and achieved successful reperfusion, defined as a modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score of 2b-3. Pre and post-EVT body temperatures were recorded. The primary outcome was favorable functional outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-2 at 90 days. Logistic regression analyses and exploratory subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the association between body temperature and clinical outcomes. RESULTS: P P P P P P Among the 219 included patients, 104 (47.5%) achieved favorable functional outcome at 90 days. Pre-EVT temperature was not significantly associated with functional outcome. In unadjusted analysis, each 1 °C increase in post-EVT temperature was associated with lower odds of favorable functional outcome (OR, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.20-0.79;= 0.01) and higher odds of mortality (OR, 2.02; 95% CI, 1.11-3.66;= 0.02). However, these associations were attenuated after multivariable adjustment (adjusted OR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.19-1.15;= 0.10; adjusted OR, 1.22; 95% CI, 0.49-3.02;= 0.67). In exploratory subgroup analyses, a potential association between higher post-EVT temperature and lower odds of favorable outcome was observed in patients with baseline NIHSS ≤ 15 (adjusted OR, 0.29; 95% CI, 0.08-0.98;= 0.047), although the interaction was not statistically significant (for interaction = 0.64). CONCLUSION: In this exploratory study, body temperature was not independently associated with functional outcome in the overall cohort. Although a potential association between higher post-EVT temperature and unfavorable outcome was observed in patients with baseline NIHSS ≤ 15, the interaction was not significant. This finding is hypothesis-generating and warrants prospective validation with pre-specified subgroup analyses.

Body temperature may constitute a potentially modifiable physiological factor associated with functional outcome. In particular, whether clinical factors, including baseline stroke severity, modify this temperature-outcome association remains uncertain.

title: A comparison of aspiration thrombectomy with catheter-directed thrombolysis in the management of Paget-Schroetter syndrome.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Acute subclavian vein thrombosis secondary to thoracic outlet syndrome (Paget-Schroetter syndrome [PSS]) requires the prompt clearing of thrombus from the subclavian vein through catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) or aspiration thrombectomy (ASP). Our goal is to systematically compare the outcomes of CDT and ASP in the management of PSS. METHODS: Consecutive patients with PSS at a single institution from 2020 through 2025 were reviewed for management with CDT or ASP. Venograms were assessed for patency, stenosis, and subclavian post-thrombotic changes (PTC). PTC were graded based on the degree of luminal encroachment and vessel irregularity: mild (<10%), moderate (10%-50%), and severe (50%-99%). Interventions were assessed: (1) within 1 week of the procedure, (2) before subclavian vein decompression, (3) 2 weeks after subclavian vein decompression, and (4) patency on the last venogram. Standardized outcomes were assessed. RESULTS: A total of 110 patients with PSS were treated over 5 years. Of these patients, 54 met the inclusion criteria: 28 underwent CDT and 26 underwent ASP. At 1 week following the procedure, rethrombosis occurred in 1 (3.6%) patient who underwent CDT and 6 (23.1%) patients who underwent ASP (P < .5). Failure to clear thrombosis occurred in 13.8% of patients who underwent ASP. The composite rate of early thrombosis and procedural failure was higher in the ASP cohort. Before PSS surgery, occlusion was noted in 1 (3.6%) patient who underwent CDT and 8 (30.8%) patients who underwent ASP (P < .05). PTC was mild in 13 (46.4%) patients receiving CDT and 5 (19.2%) receiving ASP (P < .05); moderate in 5 (17.9%) receiving CDT and 5 (19.2%) receiving ASP; and severe in 9 (32.1%) receiving CDT and 8 (30.8) receiving ASP. At early follow-up after PSS surgery, PTC was mild in 10 (43.5%) patients receiving CDT and 4 (23.5) receiving ASP; moderate in 2 (8.7%) receiving CDT and 1 (5.9%) receiving ASP; and severe in 9 (39.1%) receiving CDT and 6 (35.3%) receiving ASP. Occlusion was noted in 2 (8.7%) patients receiving CDT and 6 (35%) receiving ASP. Recanalization resulted in final patency in 22 (95%) patients receiving CDT and 15 (88%) receiving ASP. CONCLUSIONS: Both ASP and CDT may be employed for clearing thrombus in PSS; however, they differ in early efficacy, PTC, and patency. Our results suggest that while often more rapid and convenient, ASP may be inferior to CAT in the management of PSS.

Our goal is to systematically compare the outcomes of CDT and ASP in the management of PSS. METHODS: Consecutive patients with PSS at a single institution from 2020 through 2025 were reviewed for management with CDT or ASP.

title: Association of Estimated Arterial Stiffness with Collateral Status and Functional Outcome after Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Secondary Analysis of the OPTIMAL-BP Trial.
abstract: PURPOSE: Estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) is a surrogate of arterial stiffness that may influence stroke outcomes and potentially affect collateral circulation. We examined the association of ePWV with collateral status and 3-month functional outcome after successful endovascular thrombectomy and explored the contribution of collateral status to this relationship across blood pressure (BP) management strategies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this secondary analysis of the Outcome in Patients Treated With Intra-Arterial Thrombectomy-Optimal Blood Pressure Control trial, 285 patients were analyzed. Collateral status was assessed using the Tan scale (poor, 0-1; good, 2-3). Poor functional outcome was defined as 3-month modified Rankin Scale score of 3-6. Multivariable logistic and mediation analyses were performed to evaluate the association between ePWV and functional outcomes and to explore direct and indirect pathways. RESULTS: A total of 285 patients were included (mean age, 73.3±11.3 years; 40.4% women). Each 1 m/s increase in ePWV was associated with poor collaterals (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 1.276, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.083-1.503) and poor functional outcome (adjusted OR 1.338, 95% CI 1.121-1.597). In mediation analyses, collateral status accounted for only a small proportion of the association between ePWV and poor functional outcome (indirect effect: adjusted β 0.022, 95% CI 0.001-0.053), whereas the direct effect remained significant (adjusted β 0.237, 95% CI 0.115-0.359). Neither the direct effect of ePWV on functional outcome nor the indirect effect through collateral status differed according to BP management strategy. CONCLUSION: Higher ePWV was associated with poor collateral status and unfavorable functional outcome after successful reperfusion. Collateral status accounted for only a small proportion of the observed association between ePWV and functional outcome.

title: Precision medicine for futile recanalization after mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: mechanisms, diagnostics, and tailored therapies.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy has substantially improved outcomes in appropriately selected patients with acute ischemic stroke, yet futile recanalization remains a major clinical challenge. Futile recanalization describes poor functional recovery despite technically successful macrovascular reperfusion, underscoring the incomplete relationship between angiographic reperfusion and tissue-level or microvascular perfusion. This narrative review summarizes current clinical, mechanistic, and translational evidence on the determinants of futile recanalization and evaluates emerging precision-medicine approaches to its prevention and management. Precision imaging has established a role in tissue-based patient selection, and recent randomized trials have expanded thrombectomy evidence to selected patients with large-core infarction. In contrast, current randomized evidence does not support routine endovascular treatment for unselected medium-vessel occlusion populations. We further examine bridging therapy versus direct mechanical thrombectomy, individualized periprocedural management, biomarkers, and decision support based on artificial intelligence. Clinical and imaging phenotypes may provide prognostic or mechanistic information, but no phenotype-based strategy has been prospectively validated to select bridging therapy or direct thrombectomy. Biomarkers currently remain primarily prognostic or exploratory. Artificial intelligence applications are largely focused on diagnostic and prognostic support. treatment-benefit prediction, by contrast, requires evidence of treatment-effect modification and prospective validation. Experimental studies of microvascular no-reflow and thrombo-inflammation provide biological rationale for targeted interventions but do not establish clinical efficacy. Future research should integrate multimodal imaging, biological profiling, and validated decision-support tools to move beyond angiographic success toward individualized strategies focused on tissue integrity and meaningful functional recovery.

This narrative review summarizes current clinical, mechanistic, and translational evidence on the determinants of futile recanalization and evaluates emerging precision-medicine approaches to its prevention and management.

title: Drug-coated balloon, drug-eluting stent, versus bare-metal stent for vertebral artery ostial stenosis: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Stenosis at the origin of the vertebral artery (VAOS) accounts for approximately one in five posterior circulation ischemic events. Bare-metal stents (BMS) have been the conventional endovascular treatment, but restenosis occurs in 11-67% of cases. Drug-coated balloons (DCB) and drug-eluting stents (DES) are alternative strategies; however, no network meta-analysis has compared all three modalities specifically at the vertebral origin. METHODS: Five databases-PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, CNKI, and Wanfang-were searched from 2010 through May 2026 for studies comparing at least two of DCB, DES, or BMS in adults with symptomatic VAOS. The search identified 499 records; 393 underwent title and abstract screening after deduplication, from which 60 full-text articles were assessed. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was conducted using the netmeta package (R 4.5.2), with Bayesian sensitivity analysis. The primary endpoint was imaging-confirmed restenosis (≥50%). The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261413981). RESULTS: N I I 2 2 Seven studies (three randomized trials and four observational cohorts, = 970; range 46-217) met the inclusion criteria. Compared with BMS, both DES (OR 0.27, 95% CI 0.17-0.45) and DCB (OR 0.39, 95% CI 0.18-0.83) reduced restenosis. DES and DCB did not differ significantly from each other (OR 1.42, 95% CI 0.58-3.50). Between-study heterogeneity was modest (= 20.5%). Although the point estimate suggests modest heterogeneity, the wide confidence interval and the small number of studies limit precision. Lowin a small network should not be equated with clinical homogeneity. P-scores ranked DES first (88.9%), DCB second (60.7%), and BMS last (0.4%). For perioperative safety, DCB ranked highest (P-score 90.0%). CONCLUSION: Both DES and DCB reduce restenosis compared with BMS in VAOS. Both DES and DCB are associated with lower restenosis rates than BMS. The relative anti-restenosis efficacy of DES versus DCB remains uncertain due to the absence of direct head-to-head comparisons. Treatment selection should be individualized based on lesion characteristics and procedural considerations. The DCB evidence base remains small, and head-to-head comparisons of DES versus DCB at the vertebral origin are needed. title: Effect of delayed remote ischemic preconditioning on major cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events in major vascular surgery: the protocol of DRIPC randomized controlled trial.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Although endovascular therapy has become the mainstream approach for major vascular surgery, patients undergoing such procedures are still classified as high-risk according to clinical guidelines. Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) is a promising perioperative intervention strategy that has demonstrated acceptable safety and efficacy. Existing research indicates that delayed remote ischemic preconditioning (DRIPC) offers superior protective effects compared to preconditioning performed within 24 h before surgery. However, there is currently a lack of Level I evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of DRIPC in the perioperative period for vascular surgery patients. This study aims to provide high-level evidence on the effectiveness and safety of this intervention in a clinical setting. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: The trial is a single-center, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled clinical trial. A total of 1,054 patients will be recruited. The primary endpoints of the study include major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) within 30 days postoperatively. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This study has been approved by the Ethics Committee of West China Hospital of Sichuan University (approval number:2025-1846). The results will be submitted to a major clinical journal for peer review and publication. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: identifier ChiCTR2600116987.

title: Vascular Access Complexity and Thrombectomy Efficiency in Proximal MCA M1 Occlusion: Evaluation of the Bovine Aortic Arch-Dolichoarteriopathy Score.
abstract: Background and Objectives: Materials and Methods: n n Results: p p p p p Conclusions: In this study, it was aimed to investigate the relationship between the Bovine Aortic Arch-Dolichoarteriopathy (B.A.D.) score and the procedural characteristics of mechanical thrombectomy, recanalization success, and 90-day functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke with proximal M1 occlusion of the middle cerebral artery (MCA).A total of 220 adult patients who underwent mechanical thrombectomy for proximal MCA M1 occlusion were included in this retrospective, single-center cohort study. The patients were divided into good B.A.D. (<2;= 143) and poor B.A.D. (≥2;= 77) groups. Admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) and Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) scores, collateral status, thrombectomy time intervals, number of passes, first-pass effect (FPE), and Modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) recanalization grades were evaluated. The primary outcome was functional independence at day 90 (mRS 0-2). Associations with procedural and clinical outcomes were evaluated using multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses.The puncture-to-recanalization time was significantly longer in the poor B.A.D. group [67 (50.5-88.0) min vs. 43 (32.0-65.0) min,< 0.001], and the FPE rate was lower (37.7% vs. 51.7%,= 0.046). After adjustment for thrombectomy technique and clinical covariates, poor B.A.D. remained independently associated with lower odds of FPE success (aOR = 0.439, 95% CI: 0.229-0.839;= 0.013). In the procedurally adjusted linear regression model, poor B.A.D. also remained independently associated with longer puncture-to-recanalization time after additional adjustment for the number of thrombectomy passes and thrombectomy technique (B = 0.294, 95% CI: 0.188-0.400;< 0.001). Final mTICI ≥ 2b, ≥2c, and 3 recanalization rates did not differ between the groups. Although 90-day functional independence was lower in the poor B.A.D. group, the difference was not significant (51.9% vs. 63.6%,= 0.092), and no statistically significant independent association between B.A.D. status and 90-day functional independence was observed in the multivariable analysis.Poor B.A.D. anatomy was associated with greater procedural complexity during mechanical thrombectomy for proximal MCA M1 occlusion, including longer puncture-to-recanalization time and lower odds of FPE success, even after adjustment for available procedural and clinical factors. However, no statistically significant independent association was demonstrated between B.A.D. status and 90-day functional independence, and final recanalization rates did not differ significantly between the groups. These findings suggest that the B.A.D. score may have potential value as a preprocedural marker of vascular access complexity; however, prospective external validation is required before its use for procedural planning can be recommended.

title: Clinical Messages for Fenestrated Endovascular Aortic Repair from the GLOBALSTAR Registry: Outcomes in Salvage Fenestrated Endovascular Aneurysm Repair, Women, and Octogenarians.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Global Collaborators on Advanced Stent Graft Techniques for Aneurysm Repair (GLOBALSTAR) is a UK registry of complex endovascular aneurysm repair. This study aimed to examine differential outcomes after fenestrated endovascular aortic repair (FEVAR) for the following clinically relevant subgroups: women, octogenarians, and salvage FEVAR procedures to rescue previous failed repairs. METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of GLOBALSTAR. Standard comparative statistics were applied to peri-operative complications; Kaplan-Meier to survival; and cumulative incidence with competing risks to re-intervention and endoleaks. Log rank and Fine-Gray regression tests compared subgroup time to event functions. RESULTS: Over follow up of 1 651 FEVARs, salvage FEVARs experienced a significantly higher risk of re-intervention (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 1.79, 95% confidence interval [95% CI] 1.37 - 2.34; p < .001) and graft related endoleaks type 1a or 1b (sHR 2.37, 95% CI 1.45 - 3.88; p = .001) and type 3 (sHR 2.12, 95% CI 1.36 - 3.32; p = .001) than primary FEVAR. There were more secondary ruptures following salvage FEVAR (4.0% vs. 1.7%; p = .073). Women experienced double the incidence of major complication Clavien-Dindo grades 3 - 5 (22.0% vs. 11.9%; p < .001), threefold incidence of major adverse cardiovascular event (5.9% vs. 2.1%; p = .004), and peri-operative death (5.9% vs. 2.1%; p = .006) compared with men. Median survival was 5.7 years (95% CI 5.1 - 6.3) for 80 - 84 year olds and 4.8 years (95% CI 4.2 - 6.1) for ≥ 85 year olds. At one year, the overall log rank test showed no significant difference across age strata (p = .11), although octogenarians had worse one year survival than patients aged 65 - 72 years (p = .030). CONCLUSION: This study generated the following hypotheses: higher rates of re-intervention and graft related endoleak for salvage FEVAR may justify a FEVAR first strategy in appropriate cases, to achieve durable repair. Significantly worse peri-operative outcomes for women require further evaluation and may require changes in pre-operative pathways and case selection. Advanced age alone may not be a strong contraindication to FEVAR and effective case selection may yield acceptable outcomes for octogenarians. This study was limited by its retrospective design but is valuable in terms of its large real world cohort with extended follow up. The results highlight the need for dedicated prospective studies for the three subgroups, to elucidate mechanistic determinants.

METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of GLOBALSTAR.
