title: Early outcomes of the Octapro balloon-expandable transcatheter heart valve in an unrestricted cohort of patients with aortic valve stenosis: the MyPro registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Data on early outcomes of the novel balloon-expandable (BE) Octapro transcatheter heart valve (THV) in real-world practice are limited. We sought to assess procedural safety and early outcomes of the Octapro in patients with severe native aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). METHODS: Between November 2024 and October 2025, consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI with Octapro in European and Indian centres were enrolled. Primary endpoints were VARC-3 technical success, device success, and early safety at 30-day. RESULTS: 2 A total of 303 patients were included (age 78.9 ± 7.4 years; bicuspid 13%). VARC-3 technical success was 97%, peri-procedural mortality 0.3% while no procedural stroke or myocardial infarction were reported. In-hospital guidelines-indicated permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) rate was 13.5%. At discharge mean gradient was 8.4 ± 4.5 mmHg, effective orifice area 1.8 ± 0.3 cm, while moderate-to-severe paravalvular leak was reported in 3.3% of the patients. At 30-day, device success was 92.4% and early safety 80%. All-cause mortality was 2.6%, stroke 0.3%, and guidelines-indicated PPI 14.2%. Mean gradient remained low (9 ± 4 mmHg). Implantation depth and baseline right bundle branch block (RBBB) were independent predictors of PPI. ROC analysis identified an implantation depth threshold of 4.75 mm associated with increased PPI risk. CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world registry, the Octapro THV demonstrated high procedural success, favourable early clinical outcomes, and excellent haemodynamic performance. Implantation depth and baseline RBBB were independent predictors of PPI, supporting optimization of implantation technique to mitigate conduction disturbances.

title: Long-term cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in Turner syndrome patients with congenital heart disease: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Congenital cardiac anomalies are a major determinant of morbidity and mortality in Turner syndrome (TS), yet long-term cardiovascular outcome data remain limited. This study assessed cardiovascular morbidity, mortality, valve dysfunction, and aortic outcomes in TS patients with congenital cardiovascular defects. METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 84 TS patients with congenital cardiovascular anomalies were analyzed, with follow-up between 01/1980 and 01/2025. Clinical, demographic, electrocardiographic and echocardiographic variables were reviewed; morbidity and mortality were recorded; descriptive statistics applied. RESULTS: 2 Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) was present in 40 patients (48%) and coarctation of the aorta (CoA) in 29 (35%); 19 patients (23%) had both. At last follow-up (median age 26 years, IQR 31 years), most patients were in NYHA class I (82%) and mean systolic and diastolic blood pressure were 121.7 ± 16.8 mmHg and 76.1 ± 13.1 mmHg, respectively. Sinus rhythm was present in 96% of the patients. In the BAV cohort, aortic regurgitation increased from 6 patients (15%) at first registration to 17 (42.5%) at last follow-up. In the tricuspid aortic valve cohort, aortic regurgitation increased from 1 patient (2.3%) to 12 (27.9%). The last mean ascending aortic diameter indexed to body surface area was 20.4 ± 4.6 mm/m. Aortic dissection occurred in 2 patients (2.7%). Ten patients died during follow-up; median age at death was 41 years (IQR: 52 years), and cardiac causes accounted for at least 50% of mortality. CONCLUSION: BAV and CoA predominated in this TS cohort. Despite generally favorable functional status among survivors, progressive valve dysfunction, aortic complications and cardiovascular mortality support lifelong structured surveillance.

title: Analysis of risk factors and construction of a prediction model for postoperative deep vein thrombosis in patients with periarticular knee fractures.
abstract: The present study aimed to identify risk factors for postoperative deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in patients with periarticular knee fractures. A prediction model was constructed for the early identification of high-risk patients. Data from 319 patients at who underwent surgery at the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University (Luzhou, China) between January 2020 and December 2022 were analyzed. Based on ultrasound results, patients were divided into a DVT group (n=83) and a non-DVT group (n=236). Logistic regression was employed to identify independent risk factors. Subsequently, a nomogram model was established, which was validated via receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA). The DVT rate was 26.0%. Old age (OR, 1.0228), high American Society of Anesthesiologists grade (OR, 2.2764), greater blood loss (OR, 1.0015), blood transfusion (OR, 2.7917) and high D-dimer levels (OR, 1.0251) were identified as independent risk factors (P<0.05), while living in cities, high hemoglobin, high prealbumin, high Barthel index and high Braden scores served as protective factors (P<0.05). The model yielded an area under the curve value of 0.837. Additionally, the calibration curve showed high accuracy, and DCA validated the favorable clinical applicability of this predictive model. In conclusion, the model performs well in helping doctors to identify high-risk patients and optimize individualized therapeutic strategies.

title: Age-dependent patterns of D-dimer and APTT for VTE in severe pneumonia: a multicenter retrospective study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate age-stratified patterns of admission D-dimer and activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) and their complementary value for venous thromboembolism (VTE) detection in severe community-acquired pneumonia (SCAP). METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study consecutively enrolled 577 patients with SCAP admitted to two tertiary hospitals from January 2019 to December 2023. Admission coagulation parameters were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test. D-dimer values were natural log-transformed and analyzed using generalized linear models (GLMs) with a Gamma distribution and log link function. Additionally, activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), fibrinogen, prothrombin time, and international normalized ratio (INR) were fitted using Gaussian GLMs with an identity link, each adjusted for nine prespecified covariates. The independent contribution of Ln (D-dimer) to VTE was assessed through multivariable logistic regression, with discrimination evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). RESULTS: VTE occurred in 86 of 577 patients (14.9%). The VTE group demonstrated significantly higher D-dimer levels (Z = -5.785, P < 0.001). Adjusted generalized linear models (GLMs) confirmed markedly elevated Ln(D-dimer) (Wald χ² = 32.186, P < 0.001) and reduced APTT (Wald χ² = 3.935, P = 0.047) in the VTE cohort. The interaction between age and VTE did not reach statistical significance (Ln(D-dimer): P = 0.666; APTT: P = 0.075). In age-stratified analyses, significant differences in Ln (D-dimer) persisted across both age groups (both P < 0.001), whereas APTT shortening was limited to patients aged < 65 years (-5.80 s, 95% CI, -10.55 to -1.05; P = 0.017) and was not observed in those aged ≥ 65 years (-0.34 s, 95% CI, -4.06 to 3.39; P = 0.859). Ln (D-dimer) was an independent predictor of VTE (adjusted OR 2.462, 95% CI, 1.789 to 3.388, P < 0.001), with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.747 (95% CI, 0.689 to 0.805). CONCLUSION: In SCAP inpatients, VTE was linked to elevated D-dimer levels and a shortened APTT. The association with D-dimer was consistent across all age groups, whereas the shortening of APTT was primarily observed in younger patients. These age-stratified findings are exploratory due to the non-significant interaction (P = 0.075) and require prospective validation.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study consecutively enrolled 577 patients with SCAP admitted to two tertiary hospitals from January 2019 to December 2023. Admission coagulation parameters were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test.

title: Development and Internal Validation of the Si-AAA Prognostic Score for Five-Year Overall Survival after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair in Patients with Asymptomatic Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although endovascular aneurysm repair is widely used for the treatment of asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm, long-term survival is influenced by patient comorbidities and aneurysm-related characteristics. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a prognostic scoring system for predicting 5-year overall survival after endovascular aneurysm repair. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted in patients with asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm undergoing endovascular aneurysm repair. Candidate predictors included demographic, clinical, aneurysm-related, and laboratory variables. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify independent predictors of 5-year mortality. Continuous predictors were categorized using clinically interpretable thresholds derived from time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis, and a simplified point-based score was constructed from regression coefficients. Model performance was assessed using Harrell's concordance index, and internal validation was performed using 1,000 bootstrap resamples to obtain an optimism-corrected concordance index. Calibration was evaluated using bootstrap-based calibration plots. RESULTS: A total of 445 patients were screened, and 443 complete cases were included in the final analysis. During follow-up, 133 deaths (30.0%) occurred. The estimated 5-year overall survival rate was 62.8% (95% confidence interval [CI], 57.8%-68.0%). Independent predictors of 5-year mortality included age >70 years (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 1.66, 95% CI 1.06-2.62; P = 0.029), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (aHR 1.70, 95% CI 1.08-2.69; P = 0.023), unfit status (aHR 2.32, 95% CI 1.58-3.39; P < 0.001), serum albumin ≤3.5 g/dL (aHR 2.80, 95% CI 1.97-3.98; P < 0.001), and abdominal aortic aneurysm diameter ≥7 cm (aHR 1.59, 95% CI 1.07-2.38; P = 0.023). The final score ranged from 0 to 7. The apparent concordance index was 0.721, with an optimism-corrected concordance index of 0.713 after bootstrap validation. Risk stratification showed clear separation among low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups (5-year overall survival: 82.5%, 53.4%, and 23.8%, respectively; log-rank P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: A simple prognostic scoring system incorporating age, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, unfit status, serum albumin, and aneurysm diameter demonstrated acceptable discrimination and good calibration for predicting 5-year overall survival after endovascular aneurysm repair. This tool may assist in risk stratification and long-term clinical decision-making. As this score was derived and internally validated in a single-center cohort, external validation in independent cohorts is required before routine clinical implementation.

This study aimed to develop and internally validate a prognostic scoring system for predicting 5-year overall survival after endovascular aneurysm repair. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted in patients with asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm undergoing endovascular aneurysm repair.

title: Sex-Based Disparities in Statin Use and Intensity among Women with Peripheral Artery Disease: A Systematic Review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is a manifestation of systemic atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and is associated with substantial cardiovascular and limb-related morbidity. High-intensity statin therapy is recommended for patients with PAD, yet statin treatment remains underused, and sex-based differences in lipid-lowering therapy may further contribute to inequities in secondary prevention. This systematic review evaluated sex-based disparities in statxin use and statin intensity among adults with PAD. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Cochrane CENTRAL was performed from database inception through June 6, 2026. Eligible studies included adults with PAD, reported PAD-specific statin or lipid-lowering outcomes, and compared outcomes by sex. The primary outcome was high-intensity statin use among women versus men with PAD. Secondary outcomes included any statin use, no statin therapy, guideline-concordant lipid-lowering or vascular-protective therapy, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) goal achievement. Findings were synthesized narratively because of heterogeneity in study design, PAD definition, clinical setting, and outcome reporting. RESULTS: Eleven observational studies met inclusion criteria. Only two studies reported high-intensity statin use by sex, and both found lower use among women than men. In the Medicare cohort of patients with critical limb ischemia, high-intensity statin use was lower among women than men. Similarly, in the Veterans Affairs cohort, women with PAD had lower rates of high-intensity statin use, any statin use, and statin adherence. Across studies reporting secondary lipid-lowering outcomes, women were generally less likely than men to receive statins or guideline-concordant vascular-protective therapy, including in primary care, hospital discharge, revascularization, administrative claims, and vascular registry settings. LDL-C goal achievement was not reported in the included studies. CONCLUSION: Women with PAD are less likely than men to receive statin therapy and guideline-concordant vascular-protective treatment, and the limited available evidence suggests lower use of high-intensity statins among women when statin intensity is reported. These findings highlight a persistent sex-based gap in secondary prevention for PAD. Future studies should report statin intensity, adherence, LDL-C goal achievement, treatment escalation, and standardized measures of statin tolerance or intolerance separately by sex. Quality-improvement efforts should also focus on improving statin prescribing for women with PAD.

This systematic review evaluated sex-based disparities in statxin use and statin intensity among adults with PAD.

title: Antiphospholipid syndrome: epidemiology and outcomes in the evolving criteria era.
abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a heterogeneous autoimmune thrombo-inflammatory disorder characterized by thrombosis, pregnancy morbidity and an expanding spectrum of microvascular, cardiac, haematological and other systemic manifestations. Although research has provided considerable insights into the pathogenesis and clinical phenotypes of APS, its epidemiology remains difficult to define because estimates depend on case definitions, antibody testing, repeat-testing requirements, testing practices and data sources. Population-based studies suggest that APS is rare, and catastrophic APS is rarer and best understood through registry data. Antiphospholipid antibody positivity alone does not establish APS; transient or low-level positivity can occur without disease, whereas persistent antibodies must be interpreted alongside compatible clinical manifestations. Despite its rarity, APS causes substantial morbidity through recurrent thrombosis, organ damage and adverse pregnancy outcomes, supporting targeted evaluation in unprovoked or recurrent venous thromboembolism, stroke in younger adults and selected pregnancy complications. Apparent differences among populations can reflect ascertainment, access to testing, study design and biological variation. Standardized case definitions, antibody testing and laboratory reporting, together with longitudinal population-based research in ancestry-diverse, paediatric and low-income and middle-income populations, are needed to refine estimates of APS burden and define its clinical spectrum.

title: Mechanical Thrombectomy Versus Anticoagulation Alone in Intermediate-High Risk PE: Improved Functional 90-Day Outcomes in STORM-PE RCT.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Up to 50% of pulmonary embolism (PE) survivors experience long-term functional limitations and reduced quality of life (QoL). Reperfusion strategies can rapidly relieve right-ventricular (RV) dysfunction and prevent clinical deterioration or hemodynamic collapse; however, these approaches have never been evaluated in a randomized trial against anticoagulation alone using patient-centered outcomes. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate whether mechanical thrombectomy with anticoagulation improves functional, QoL, and safety outcomes compared with anticoagulation alone in patients with acute intermediate-high risk PE over 90 days. METHODS: STORM-PE enrolled 100 PE patients randomized 1:1 to computer-assisted vacuum thrombectomy (CAVT) with anticoagulation or anticoagulation alone across 22 international sites, with RV-to-left-ventricular (RV/LV) ratio change at 48 hours as the primary endpoint. Secondary endpoints included major adverse events within 7 days, functional and QoL outcomes, mortality, and symptomatic PE recurrence through 90 days. RESULTS: For all patients, median time from randomization to last follow-up visit was 91.0 days [Q1-Q3: 80.5-100.0]. At 90 days, 66.0% (31/47) of CAVT and 64.2% (34/53) of anticoagulation patients completed the 6-min walk test. The CAVT arm exhibited a longer 6-min walk distance compared with anticoagulation alone (478.7 ± 159.5 m vs 368.0 ± 127.8 m, P = 0.003). More CAVT than anticoagulation patients were NYHA functional class I (97.4% [37/38] vs 75.6% [34/45], P = 0.005) at 90 days. Dyspnea and QoL scores were comparable between groups, with no differences between arms for all-cause mortality, PE-related mortality, and symptomatic PE recurrence within 90 days. CONCLUSIONS: In STORM-PE, CAVT with anticoagulation resulted in improved functional outcomes at 90 days compared with anticoagulation alone, with equivalent safety rates. This trial supports CAVT as an effective and safe reperfusion strategy for intermediate-high risk PE. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov Unique Identifier: NCT05684796.

title: Recanalisation quality, not first-pass effect, drives outcomes in paediatric mechanical thrombectomy: a multicentre prospective study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: In adult endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), first-pass success is associated with better outcomes, but whether this "first-pass effect" also holds true in childhood stroke remains unknown. We investigated the association of thrombectomy pass counts with 90-day outcomes after paediatric EVT. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analysed prospectively collected data from the international Save ChildS Pro registry (ages 0-17 years). All EVT-treated patients were included irrespective of the reperfusion grade achieved. Successful reperfusion was defined as expanded thrombolysis in cerebral infarction (eTICI) ≥ 2b and complete/near-complete reperfusion as eTICI 2c-3. The primary outcome was ordinal 90-day mRS in a proportional odds model. Single-pass and multiple-pass patients were then compared with each other within the subgroup achieving eTICI 2c-3. Logistic regression for mRS > 2 was fitted with pass count and eTICI grade as covariates. RESULTS: Of 103 patients (median age 11 years [IQR 6-15]; 55/102 [53.9%] male), median passes were 2 (IQR 1-3); 39 (37.9%) had 1 pass, 61 (59.2%) more than 1 and 3 (2.9%) recanalised without a thrombectomy pass. Multiple passes were associated with lower eTICI 2c-3 rates (30.0% vs 82.1%; P < .001), and worse 90-day mRS (common odds ratio 3.47; 95% CI, 1.63-7.38; P = .001). However, among patients achieving eTICI 2c-3 (n = 50), we detected no difference by pass count (mRS 0-2: 93.8% vs 94.4%; risk difference - 0.6%, 95% CI, -15% to +20%; P = 1.000). After accounting for eTICI, pass count was not independently associated with mRS > 2, while eTICI remained significant. CONCLUSIONS: In this analysis of the first-pass effect in paediatric thrombectomy, multiple passes were associated with worse functional outcomes, but this effect appeared to be largely mediated through recanalisation quality. Subgroup analyses were underpowered to exclude a clinically relevant residual effect of pass count, and these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating.

We investigated the association of thrombectomy pass counts with 90-day outcomes after paediatric EVT. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analysed prospectively collected data from the international Save ChildS Pro registry (ages 0-17 years).

title: Comparative Outcomes of Carotid Artery Stenting, Transcarotid Artery Revascularization, and Carotid Endarterectomy in Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis: A Propensity-Matched Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To compare myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, mortality, and major adverse events (MAEs) after carotid artery stenting (CAS), transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), and carotid endarterectomy (CEA). METHODS: Using TriNetX, adults undergoing CAS, TCAR, or CEA for asymptomatic carotid stenosis from 2015 to 2025 were identified using International Classification of Diseases 10th Edition Procedure Coding System (ICD-10-PCS) codes. Asymptomatic status required no stroke or transient ischemic attack within 6 months before surgery. Propensity score matching was performed for CAS versus TCAR (5,558 pairs), TCAR versus CEA (9,666 pairs), and CAS versus CEA (13,707 pairs). Outcomes through 1 year were assessed using risk ratios (RRs) kand Kaplan-Meier analyses. RESULTS: At 1 year, CAS was associated with higher stroke risk than TCAR (5.16% vs 3.74%; RR 1.31; P = 0.002) and CEA (4.92% vs 3.47%; RR 1.44; P < 0.001), whereas TCAR and CEA were similar (3.91% vs 3.79%; P = 0.52). CAS had lower mortality than TCAR (3.78% vs 7.65%; RR 0.49; P < 0.001), but mortality was similar in the other comparisons. MI was lower after CAS than TCAR (2.03% vs 2.95%; RR 0.63; P < 0.001), with no differences otherwise. MAE was higher after CAS than CEA (7.66% vs 6.46%; RR 1.20; P < 0.001), but similar between CAS and TCAR and between TCAR and CEA. CONCLUSION: Among patients selected for revascularization, CAS was associated with higher stroke risk than TCAR and CEA, lower MI and mortality than TCAR, and higher MAE than CEA. These observational findings complement randomized evidence and require cautious interpretation given residual confounding and unavailable anatomic data.

title: Early Results of Shape Memory Polymer Embolization for Endoleak Treatment after Thoracoabdominal Fenestrated/Branched Endovascular Aneurysm Repair.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endoleaks after thoracoabdominal fenestrated/branched endovascular aneurysm repair (TA-F/BEVAR) may require multimodal treatment, including sac access and cavity filling. Shape memory polymer (SMP) is a self-expanding porous scaffold that promotes organized thrombus, is radiolucent, exerts low radial force, and biodegrades. We evaluated SMP embolization to fill endoleak cavities after TA-F/BEVAR. METHODS: Retrospective review of all patients treated at a single center with IMPEDE-FX Embolization Plugs for endoleak after TA-F/BEVAR (July 2024-June 2026). Outcomes were endoleak resolution, change in sac diameter and volume, complications, and endoleak-related reintervention. RESULTS: Ten patients (8 male; median age 70) underwent 12 procedures. The median preoperative endoleak volume was 25 mL (range, 3-148 mL); 6 had prior endoleak-directed reintervention. A median 114 plugs were implanted per procedure (range, 29-297). No procedural complications occurred. At a median of 34 days, 5 patients (50%) had complete resolution, 3 (30%) near-complete resolution (residual 1.3-2.0 mL), and 2 (20%) partial resolution (residual 25-32 mL); both of the latter underwent a second SMP procedure achieving near-complete resolution. At last follow-up (median 155 days; range, 30-761 days) no new endoleaks were identified. Sacs regressed in 6 patients and were stable in 4; none expanded. CONCLUSION: SMP embolization was safe and effective for significant endoleak after TA-F/BEVAR, despite large endoleak volumes and frequent prior failed intervention. All patients achieved substantial endoleak reduction or resolution; most sacs regressed and none expanded. Longer follow-up is needed to establish durability.

title: Failure Modes of Endovascular Therapy for Spontaneous Isolated Superior Mesenteric Artery Dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mechanisms of failure after endovascular stenting for symptomatic spontaneous isolated superior mesenteric artery dissection (SISMAD) remain poorly characterized. We analyzed device- and procedure-related failure modes in a 17-year single-center cohort. METHODS: We reviewed 117 consecutive patients with SISMAD (2008-2025). Patients stented for persistent or escalating pain despite conservative management formed the cohort; catheter-infusion and open-surgery patients were analyzed separately. Lesions were classified by Yun morphology. Failure modes were classified a priori as type I (intraprocedural technical failure), type II (thrombotic events occurring after the procedure), and type III (in-stent restenosis or intimal hyperplasia at ≥6 months). Patency and reinterventions were recorded. RESULTS: Thirty-two patients underwent endovascular therapy (28 stenting, 4 catheter-directed infusion). In the stent cohort, uncomplicated technical success was 82.1% (23/28). Type I failures occurred in 17.9% (5/28), dominated by false-lumen deployment (10.7%) clustered in Yun III occlusions (50.0% vs. 9.1%; P = 0.050). Type II events (3 weeks; 24 months) were rescued by reintervention. Type III events developed in 22.7% (5/22), confined to multi-stent constructs (45.5% vs. 0%; P = 0.035). Primary patency was 81.8% (18/22) at a median 19-month imaging follow-up; secondary patency was 100% after 3 reinterventions. Greater baseline true-lumen stenosis and Yun III morphology predicted composite events. No patient died; the only bowel resection preceded secondary stenting. CONCLUSION: Endovascular therapy for SISMAD fails in characteristic, morphology-dependent patterns. The proposed three-type classification is exploratory and requires validation in larger cohorts.

title: Macrophage-mediated inflammation and microcalcification are associated with abdominal aortic aneurysm progression and clinical events.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Molecular and cellular imaging biomarkers of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) show promise as potential predictors of clinical events. This study assessed long-term clinical outcomes using ultrasmall superparamagnetic particles of iron oxide (USPIO)-enhanced MRI (ISRCTN76413758) and fluorine-18 sodium fluoride ([18F]NaF) PET/CT (NCT02229006). METHODS: In two prospective multicentre co-enrolled observational cohort studies of patients with asymptomatic AAAs, evaluation of aortic wall inflammation using USPIO-enhanced MRI in 338 patients was followed by [18F]NaF PET/CT in a subgroup of 72 patients, to evaluate microcalcification. Aneurysms were classified according to aortic wall USPIO enhancement and into tertiles of [18F]NaF uptake. Aneurysm expansion, composite of rupture or repair, and overall survival were compared. RESULTS: In 338 predominantly elderly (mean(s.d.) age of 73.5(7.2) years) men (85.2%) with a mean(s.d.) aneurysm diameter of 49.5(7.3) mm, aneurysm expansion was increased in patients with USPIO enhancement (median of 3.3 (interquartile range (i.q.r.) 2.0-4.6) versus 2.5 (i.q.r. 1.4-3.6) mm/year; P = 0.002) or high [18F]NaF uptake (median of 4.0 (i.q.r. 2.6-5.4) versus 1.9 (i.q.r. 0.9-3.0) mm/year; P < 0.001), even when adjusted for hypertension, smoking, and baseline AAA diameter (P = 0.038 and P = 0.003). After a median follow-up of 102 (i.q.r. 58-119) months, 62.7% of patients met the composite endpoint of rupture or repair, with high [18F]NaF uptake associated with a more than two-fold higher risk (72% versus 36%; log rank P = 0.002). There was no association between USPIO enhancement and future rupture or repair. CONCLUSION: Aortic wall USPIO enhancement and [18F]NaF uptake are independently associated with AAA expansion. These non-invasive imaging biomarkers provide an opportunity to identify those at the greatest risk of AAA progression and may help inform further research to determine optimal surveillance intervals.

title: Use of smart glasses for ultrasound-guided central venous catheterization in adults: a randomized clinical trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Head-mounted displays can be integrated with ultrasonography to overlay the image in the operator's field of view, improving hand-eye coordination during invasive procedures. The clinical efficacy of smart glasses for central venous catheterization (CVC) remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate whether using smart glasses can improve efficiency compared to conventional ultrasound-guided CVC. METHODS: This prospective, single-blinded, controlled study enrolled adult patients who underwent elective surgery requiring CVC. Patients were assigned to either the ultrasound screen (control) or smart glasses group using stratified randomization according to operator qualification. The primary outcome was the overall CVC procedural time. Secondary outcomes included ultrasound scanning and venous access time, number of needle redirections and probe repositionings, procedural success and complication rates. RESULTS: In total, 124 patients were analyzed. The overall procedural time was significantly reduced in the smart glasses group compared to that in the control group (158 [140, 189] s vs. 134 [117,150] s; median difference, 26.0 s; 95% CI, [16.0-37.0] s, P < 0.001). Specifically, the ultrasound scanning time (median difference, 3.0 s, P = 0.004), venous access time (median difference, 2.0 s, P = 0.013), number of needle redirections (median difference, 1.0, P = 0.003) and probe repositionings (median difference, 0.0, P = 0.005) were significantly reduced in the smart glasses group compared to those in the control group. However, the success and complication rates were comparable between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Smart glasses modestly improved procedural efficiency in ultrasound-guided CVC, potientially for novices, without improving success or complication rates. Larger-sample studies with more diverse operators and patients are warranted. title: Sequential Arch-Tear Eligibility for Uncovered Aortic Arch Stent in Acute DeBakey Type I Aortic Dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Because an uncovered arch scaffold does not provide a covered seal across an unresected arch tear, we evaluated a source-adjudicated sequential eligibility framework separating study-defined stop gates from residual-risk modifiers. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 266 patients with acute DeBakey type I dissection treated by hemiarch repair alone (No. = 160) or hemiarch plus AMDS (No. = 106). Blinded preoperative CT-scan re-review validated Gate 1 (visible arch tear), and operative-report review confirmed Gate 2 (tear directly observed at open inspection). Supra-aortic false-lumen communication was assessed only after both gates were negative. RESULTS: p p p Sixty-nine patients (25.9%) passed both study-defined gates (AMDS = 32; hemiarch = 37). Twelve-month CT-scan was available in 45/69 (65.2%; AMDS 24/32, hemiarch 21/37). Among imaged patients, complete zone 2-3 false-lumen exclusion occurred in 20/24 (83.3%) after AMDS and 0/21 after hemiarch (risk difference +83.3 percentage points, 95% CI +58.7 to +93.3;< 0.001). DANE occurred in 4/32 (12.5%) and 16/37 (43.2%), respectively (= 0.007). Under the adverse opposing missingness scenario, the exclusion risk difference narrowed to +19.3 percentage points (95% CI -4.2 to +39.9;= 0.148). CONCLUSIONS: These findings are hypothesis-generating and apply to a selected post hoc subgroup; treatment comparisons are non-causal. Prospective external validation of the study-defined hierarchy remains required.

title: Management of Brachial Plexus Neurogenic Tumors: A Retrospective Study of 25 Cases.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: To investigate the clinical characteristics of cervical brachial plexus neurogenic tumors and enhance the diagnostic and therapeutic management of this condition. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of 25 patients diagnosed with brachial plexus neurogenic tumors who were treated at a tertiary teaching hospital between January 2019 and December 2024. Clinical manifestations, treatment strategies, and follow-up outcomes were systematically summarized. RESULTS: A total of 25 patients were included, treated across multiple departments: otorhinolaryngology-head and neck surgery, neurosurgery, orthopedics, thyroid surgery, and vascular surgery. There were 13 male and 12 female patients, aged 16-76 y, with a disease duration ranging from 1 wk to 2 y, defined as the interval from symptom onset to initial clinical evaluation. The primary presenting symptom was a neck root mass in 21 patients, among whom seven experienced ipsilateral upper limb numbness, soreness, or electric shock-like pain upon palpation and four reported sensory disturbances in the upper extremity or shoulder-back pain. All patients underwent cervical contrast-enhanced computed tomography, and 18 additionally received 3.0 T magnetic resonance imaging. Preoperative ultrasound-guided fine needle aspiration cytology was performed in all cases, revealing spindle cell tumors with morphological features suggestive of schwannoma. Of the 25 patients, 23 underwent surgical resection, while two with small tumors (<2 cm), no neurological symptoms, and cytologically benign findings opted for conservative management with close observation. Surgical approaches included the anterior supraclavicular approach, the posterior cervical paravertebral approach, and clavicle-splitting (transclavicular) approach. Postoperative pathological examination confirmed benign schwannoma in 22 cases and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor in one case. Follow-up duration ranged from 12 to 60 mo. Transient postoperative neurological dysfunction occurred in five patients, manifesting as limited shoulder abduction, reduced wrist extensor strength, or limb numbness; all deficits resolved within 6 mo following structured rehabilitation programs. CONCLUSIONS: Brachial plexus neurogenic tumors commonly present as a mass in the neck root, with a subset of cases accompanied by neurological symptoms. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging are valuable modalities for tumor localization and qualitative characterization. Preoperative fine needle aspiration cytology enables a preliminary assessment of tumor histology. The selection of an appropriate surgical approach should be guided by tumor location and anatomical involvement. Intralesional enucleation is a key strategy for preserving neurological function, and when combined with microsurgical techniques and intraoperative nerve monitoring, even transient postoperative neurological deficits can be effectively managed through structured rehabilitation programs.

title: Baricitinib Efficacy Through 4 Years in Responders and Safety up to 5 Years in Adults with Severe Alopecia Areata: Final Results from BRAVE-AA1 and BRAVE-AA2.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Long-term efficacy and safety data are imperative for therapies used to treat severe alopecia areata (AA) because the disease is chronic, loss of response can be devastating to patients, and the safety profile needs to support long-term therapy. Baricitinib, a selective JAK inhibitor, has been approved for severe AA in adults and is being studied in pediatric patients. This study evaluates the final long-term efficacy and safety of baricitinib in adults with severe AA. METHODS: Efficacy was assessed for patients randomized to baricitinib 4 mg or 2 mg who achieved response (Severity of Alopecia Tool [SALT] score ≤ 20) at Week 52 (4 mg, N = 133; 2 mg, N = 72) and stayed on the same dose through Week 200. Proportions of patients maintaining a SALT score ≤ 20 and achieving a Clinician-Reported Outcome Measure for Eyebrow/Eyelash (EB/EL) Hair Loss™ score of 0 or 1 with ≥ 2-point improvement from baseline were reported using the modified last-observation-carried-forward method. Safety is reported as incidence rates (IR) per 100 patient-years at risk for the All BARI AA group (N = 1303) and Extended BARI AA group (N = 948) through 248 weeks of exposure RESULTS: For baricitinib 4 mg and 2 mg, respectively, among Week 52 responders, 115/133 (86.5%) and 61/72 (84.7%) maintained a SALT score ≤ 20 at Week 200. Regrowth of EB/EL hair continued beyond Week 52 and was maintained through Week 200. In up to 5 years of exposure with baricitinib, the IR for serious infections, nonmelanoma skin cancer malignancies, deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolism, and major adverse cardiovascular events remained low relative to background rates. No deaths occurred, and adverse event rates remained stable over time. CONCLUSIONS: Within this population, ~ 85% of responders maintained SALT scores ≤ 20 through approximately 4 years with continued benefit for EB/EL. Baricitinib's safety profile remained consistent over 5 years of treatment, in line with prior BRAVE program findings. englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Long-term efficacy and safety data are imperative for therapies used to treat severe alopecia areata (AA) because the disease is chronic, loss of response can be devastating to patients, and the safety profile needs to support long-term therapy. Baricitinib, a selective JAK inhibitor, has been approved for severe AA in adults and is being studied in pediatric patients. This study evaluates the final long-term efficacy and safety of baricitinib in adults with severe AA.

title: Artificial Intelligence in 3D Aortic CTA Segmentation for Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Management: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) is the reference imaging modality for diagnosis, endovascular planning, and surveillance of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs), but conventional assessment remains time-consuming, operator-dependent, and limited by complex anatomy. This narrative review examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in three-dimensional aortic CTA segmentation for AAA management. The narrative synthesis drew on literature identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and the Cochrane Library, with the original search covering January 2000 to July 2026. Ten primary studies from the existing bibliography were characterized in a study-level table, and reported Dice coefficients were displayed for nine studies. Current evidence indicates that AI-based segmentation, particularly using convolutional neural networks, U-Net-derived models, and nnU-Net frameworks, can improve the speed and reproducibility of aortic lumen, wall, thrombus, branch vessel, endograft, and aneurysm sac delineation. These techniques may support more accurate morphometric measurements, device sizing, procedural planning, quantitative surveillance, and the development of advanced imaging biomarkers. However, available studies remain heterogeneous in datasets, anatomical evaluation, imaging protocols, validation strategies, and reported performance metrics, limiting direct comparison and clinical generalizability. AI-assisted 3D segmentation represents a promising tool for transforming CTA from descriptive imaging into quantitative decision support, but robust multicenter validation, workflow integration, and expert supervision remain essential before widespread clinical adoption.

title: Selective endovascular aortic repair in connective tissue disease patients within a multidisciplinary program achieves comparable outcomes in high-risk patients.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Endovascular aortic repair (ENDO) in patients with connective tissue disease (CTD) has historically been discouraged in society guidelines because of durability concerns. However, high-volume aortic centers increasingly employ ENDO strategies in carefully selected high-risk patients across scenarios such as rupture, dissection-related pathology, or hostile anatomy. Herein, we describe temporal ENDO adoption at our multidisciplinary CTD aortic program. METHODS: In this study, 92 patients with CTD undergoing aortic intervention at a single high-volume aortic center between 2005 and 2023 were analyzed. Patients were stratified by ENDO (n = 50) vs open repair (OPEN; n = 42). The primary outcome was freedom from aortic-related mortality (ARM). The secondary outcomes included technical success, complications, secondary aortic intervention (SAI), and overall survival. A prespecified contemporary analysis (2018-2023) was conducted to evaluate the outcomes following the establishment of a multidisciplinary CTD aortic program. The Kaplan-Meier method was used to estimate survival and freedom from SAI. RESULTS: The mean age was 48 ± 16 years, and 34% (n = 31) were female. Diagnoses included Marfan syndrome (69%), Loeys-Dietz syndrome (15%), familial aortopathy (11%), and vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (5%). Patients who underwent ENDO more frequently had prior sternotomy/open cardiac surgery (68% vs 19%; P < .0001), prior aortic surgery (70% vs 33%; P = .0007), and urgent presentation (50% vs 14%; P = .0004). Overall, 60% of these patients were deemed unfit for open repair by the multidisciplinary aortic team because of physiologic risk, anatomic complexity, or urgent presentation. The technical success rate was lower after ENDO (82% vs 98%; P = .02), and the 30-day reintervention rate was higher (16% vs 0%; P = .01). The median follow-up period was 2.3 years [interquartile range, 1.1-4.7]. SAIs occurred more frequently following ENDO (56% vs 12%; P = .0001), including planned staged procedures (ENDO: 28.6% vs OPEN: 20%; P = 1) and unplanned reinterventions (ENDO: 71.4% vs OPEN: 80%; P = 1). In the full cohort, patients undergoing ENDO had lower 3-year survival rates (71% ± 7% vs 92% ± 4%; log-rank P = .03). In the contemporary cohort, survival at 2 years following ENDO (n = 17) was poorer than that after OPEN (n = 42), although the difference did not reach significance (71% ± 14% vs 92% ± 4%; log-rank P = .1). Similarly, the rate of freedom from ARM was lower, but not significantly different (88% ± 12% vs 98% ± 2%; log-rank P = .4). CONCLUSIONS: Open repair remains the gold standard for connective tissue disease-associated aortic disease. In carefully selected high-risk patients, ENDO serves as a complementary strategy with acceptable contemporary survival and comparable freedom from ARM. Higher secondary intervention rates reflect both planned staged repair and unplanned surveillance-detected failure modes, underscoring the need for lifelong follow-up within multidisciplinary programs.

title: Beyond the Threshold: Continuous Creatinine Change and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy for Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) worsens outcomes in acute ischemic stroke, but threshold-based definitions do not capture prognostic information from subthreshold changes. We tested whether early creatinine change within 48 hours of EVT conveys graded prognostic information beyond dichotomous CA-AKI. METHODS: We performed a secondary analysis of the CAN-REST registry (Contrast-Associated Nephropathy After Endovascular Stroke Treatment), a retrospective multicenter observational cohort study of 6638 EVT-treated adults with acute ischemic stroke enrolled at 73 centers in 16 countries between January 1 and December 31, 2023. Early creatinine change was quantified as the natural logarithm ratio of 48-hour creatinine to baseline creatinine (ln[48-hour/baseline creatinine]), with CA-AKI defined per Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes criteria (≥0.3 mg/dL or ≥1.5× baseline rise within 48 hours). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for prespecified baseline and periprocedural covariates examined associations with 90-day modified Rankin Scale shift and in-hospital mortality; linear versus restricted cubic spline specification was selected by likelihood ratio testing, and contrasts were estimated at ±10%, ±25%, and ±50%. RESULTS: Greater creatinine worsening within 48 hours of EVT was independently associated with an unfavorable 90-day modified Rankin Scale shift (adjusted common odds ratio per 1-unit log-ratio increase, 1.48 [95% CI, 1.07-2.04]; linear) and in-hospital mortality (nonlinear dose-response, of larger magnitude). A 10% increase in creatinine at 48 hours-well below Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes threshold-was associated with worse functional outcome (adjusted common odds ratio, 1.04 [95% CI, 1.01-1.07]) and death (adjusted odds ratio, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.13-1.32]); a 10% decrease in creatinine at 48 hours was associated with lower odds of both outcomes (adjusted common odds ratio, 0.96 [95% CI, 0.93-0.99]; adjusted odds ratio, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.65-0.86]). The functional-outcome association concentrated at upper modified Rankin Scale cut-points (severe disability, death); effect modification by baseline renal function was not significant. CONCLUSIONS: Early creatinine change after EVT conveys graded, outcome-specific prognostic information extending below formal CA-AKI thresholds, with a dose-response detectable at changes as modest as ±10%, complementing binary CA-AKI as a framework for post-EVT renal risk assessment. title: Comparison of recommendations for initial adult traumatic brain injury management across clinical practice guidelines and consensus statements: a scoping review.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide. We conducted a scoping review to identify, map, and compare recommendations for the initial medical management of adult TBI. METHODS: Following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR, we searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, guideline repositories, and gray literature for English or Spanish language documents published from 2010 to 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records, charted recommendations across domains, and rated agreement using a priori categories; discrepancies were resolved by consensus or third reviewer. RESULTS: Sixteen documents met inclusion criteria, including guidelines, consensus statements, and best-practice recommendations. Broad agreement existed for early neurological assessment, airway protection, avoidance of hypotension and hypoxemia, and timely neuroimaging. Heterogeneity remained in blood pressure and cerebral perfusion pressure targets, repeat imaging, definitions of neurological deterioration, escalation criteria, observation protocols, and discharge processes. Anticonvulsant prophylaxis and venous thromboembolism prevention were inconsistently addressed. Blood-based biomarkers appeared in only three documents and were limited to computed tomography decision-making. CONCLUSIONS: Although the fundamental principles of care were largely consistent, important differences remain in their operational implementation. Greater harmonization of clinical definitions and management pathways may facilitate more consistent application of evidence-based recommendations across healthcare settings.

title: AngioJet rheolytic thrombectomy under superior vena cava filter protection for acute upper extremity deep vein thrombosis in patients with cancer: a single-center, retrospective analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The incidence of upper extremity deep vein thrombosis (UEDVT) is increasing, and percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy (PMT) is receiving more attention as a treatment option. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and clinical outcomes of PMT combined with superior vena cava (SVC) filter protection in cancer patients with acute UEDVT. METHODS: This study included all patients with acute UEDVT who underwent treatment with an 8-Fr AngioJet thrombectomy system (Boston Scientific) under the protection of a retrievable SVC filter between January 1, 2020, and October 1, 2025. The evaluation indicators included technical success rate (defined as a thrombus clearance rate >80%), intraoperative adverse events, degree of limb swelling relief, incidence of pulmonary embolism, and thrombus recurrence during follow-up. RESULTS: A total of 19 patients (10 female; mean age 60.84 ± 11.30 years) were included. All patients had secondary UEDVT and a history of malignant tumors, with 14 cases (73.7%) having a history of central venous catheterization. All procedures achieved technical success, with no severe adverse events such as major bleeding occurring intraoperatively, nor were there any new symptomatic pulmonary embolisms. The average circumference of the affected limb 10 cm above the elbow before surgery was 29.83 ± 2.20 cm, which decreased to 26.98 ± 2.0 cm on the second postoperative day. During the 6-month follow-up, one patient with advanced lung cancer developed swelling of the upper limb on postoperative day 136, confirmed by ultrasound to be a recurrence of deep vein thrombosis; another patient was found to have an asymptomatic mural thrombus on ultrasound examination on postoperative day 28. CONCLUSION: PMT with the 8-Fr AngioJet system and SVC filter protection appears to be a safe and effective treatment option for cancer patients with acute UEDVT.

title: Perioperative Lactate, Survival, and Complications Following Lung Transplantation.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To examine perioperative lactate and its association with survival and postoperative complications following lung transplantation (LTx). DESIGN: Single-center retrospective cohort study. SETTING: Academic tertiary-care transplant center. PARTICIPANTS: Adult patients undergoing LTx between February 2018 and January 2023. INTERVENTIONS: None. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Serum lactate was measured at 6-hour intervals from the start of surgery, and the maximum value within the first 0 to 6 hours was recorded. Patients were categorized into the high-lactate group (upper quartile, ≥4.2 mmol/L) and low-lactate group (lower 3 quartiles). Primary outcomes were 1-year and overall survival. Secondary outcomes included renal failure, venous thromboembolism (VTE), primary graft dysfunction grade 3 (PGD3), mechanical ventilation duration, intensive care unit (ICU) and post-transplant length of stay, and in-hospital mortality. Among 225 recipients (median age, 62.3 years; 34.2% female), high lactate was not associated with 1-year or overall survival. However, recipients with high lactate had higher rates of PGD3 at 72 hours (42.1% v 13.1%, p < 0.001), longer mechanical ventilation duration (3 days v 2 days, p = 0.003), longer ICU stay (11.6 days v 7 days, p = 0.013), and higher in-hospital mortality rate (7% v 0.6%, p = 0.019). No significant differences were observed in renal failure, VTE, or post-transplant length of stay. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated perioperative serum lactate was associated with PGD3 at 72 hours, prolonged mechanical ventilation, longer ICU stay, and in-hospital mortality but not 1-year or overall survival following LTx. These findings suggest that perioperative lactate may aid in identifying high-risk patients early in their postoperative course despite its lack of association with long-term survival.

title: Hemodynamic Analysis of Modified Splenic Arteriovenous Shunt in Pancreas Transplantation.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a modified splenic arteriovenous shunt technique in pancreas transplantation through intraoperative hemodynamic monitoring and postoperative follow-up. METHODS: A total of 12 patients undergoing simultaneous pancreas-kidney transplantation were enrolled. Under three consecutive intraoperative states (spleen preserved, splenic arteriovenous clamped, and splenic arteriovenous shunt created), color Doppler ultrasound was used to measure peak systolic velocity (PS) and volumetric flow (VF) of the splenic artery and vein at the same point in the distal pancreatic tail, while portal venous pressure was recorded using an intravascular pressure transducer. Postoperative graft function, thrombotic events, and complications were regularly followed up. RESULTS: Compared with the spleen-preserved state, the clamped state showed significant reductions in splenic arterial PS and VF (15.24 ± 4.43 cm/s, 16.62 ± 6.84 mL/min) and splenic venous PS and VF (16.31 ± 3.82 cm/s, 60.32 ± 16.07 mL/min) (P < 0.001). In the shunt state, splenic arterial (54.47 ± 3.45 cm/s, 157.39 ± 11.24 mL/min) and venous (49.27 ± 6.61 cm/s, 177.89 ± 14.15 mL/min) flow parameters showed no significant differences compared with the spleen-preserved state (P > 0.05), but were significantly higher than those in the clamped state (P < 0.001). Portal venous pressure showed no significant differences among the three states (P > 0.05). At a median follow-up of 5 months, no graft thrombosis, pancreatitis, or gastrointestinal bleeding was observed, and patient and graft survival rates were both 100% at the last follow-up. Glycated hemoglobin decreased from 7.37% ± 0.68% preoperatively to 5.81% ± 0.32% (P < 0.005), and left ventricular ejection fraction increased from 59.50% ± 3.23% to 67.33% ± 2.84% (P < 0.005). CONCLUSION: The modified splenic arteriovenous shunt maintains physiological perfusion of the pancreatic allograft without elevating portal venous pressure, and may mitigate the hypoperfusion and blood stasis associated with conventional splenic vessel ligation. Based on the short-term results of this study, this modified technique appears safe and feasible, and may contribute to reducing early thrombotic complications after pancreas transplantation.

title: Vascular Management Strategies and Outcomes of Infectious Arterial Complications Involving the Kidney Transplant Vasculature: A Systematic Review and Evidence-Informed Treatment Framework.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Infectious arterial complications involving the kidney transplant (KT) vasculature are rare but life-threatening and frequently result in KT loss. The lack of evidence-based guidance for vascular management strategies underscores the need for systematic synthesis to inform clinical decision-making. METHODS: A systematic search was performed from database inception through August 22, 2025, for reports of culture-proven infectious vascular complications-including arterial rupture, detachment, pseudoaneurysm, aneurysm, thrombosis, or stenosis-involving the transplant renal artery, iliac vessels, or arterial anastomosis in KT recipients. Eligible studies reported vascular management strategies. Due to methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively using proportion-based comparisons. RESULTS: Eighty reports (1972-2025) comprising 139 cases were included. Candida species were most frequent, followed by Pseudomonas, Aspergillus, and Staphylococcus species. Pseudoaneurysm and arterial rupture were the predominant clinical presentation, typically occuring within the first month after transplantation. Outcome patterns differed by transplant nephrectomy status, with vascular management strategies performed without transplant nephrectomy demonstrating higher reported proportions of uneventful follow-up. Autologous interposition grafting demonstrated the most favorable outcome pattern (86.7% uneventful recovery; 6.7% reintervention and mortality), even when transplant nephrectomy is unavoidable. Covered stent placement was the most frequently reported intervention andshowed favorable outcomes in selected KT-preserving cases (75% uneventful recovery). Primary surgical repair had the highest reintervention proportion (59.1%), whereas arterial ligation had the highest mortality (43.8%) and accounted for all reported limb loss. CONCLUSION: Across five decades of case-based evidence, autologous interposition grafting demonstrated the most favorable outcome pattern and may represent the preferred vascular management strategy when durable arterial reconstruction is feasible, including when transplant nephrectomy is required. Covered stent placement may provide a useful option in selected cases or as a temporizing strategy for hemorrhage control. These findings should guide rather than define management decisions given the heterogeneous evidence base. HIGHLIGHTS: First systematic synthesis of management strategies for infectious arterial complications involving the kidney transplant vasculature Candida was the most frequently reported pathogen; pseudoaneurysm and arterial rupture were the predominant presentations Vascular management strategies performed without transplant nephrectomy demonstrated higher reported proportions of uneventful follow-up Autologous interposition grafting showed the most favorable reported outcome pattern, even when transplant nephrectomy is unavoidable Ligation and primary repair were associated with higher reported mortality and reintervention, respectively.

title: Intended Thrombectomy for Basilar Artery Occlusion with Mild Deficits: Evidence from a Multicenter Prospective Registry.
abstract: P Supplemental material is available for this article. Background The role of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) in basilar artery occlusion (BAO) with mild deficits (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] score < 10) remains uncertain. Purpose To compare the outcomes of EVT combined with best medical management (BMM) versus BMM alone in individuals with BAO and mild deficits. Materials and Methods Consecutive eligible patients treated at eight stroke centers between September 2023 and March 2025 were enrolled in a prospective registry. The primary outcome was 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] score of 0-2). Secondary outcomes were 90-day excellent outcome (mRS score of 0-1), death, and early neurologic deterioration (END), defined as a four-point or greater increase in NIHSS score within 72 hours. Primary analyses followed an intention-to-treat-like framework with inverse probability weighting (IPW). As-treated and per-protocol sensitivity analyses were used to assess the robustness of the results and the impact of treatment crossover (EVT after END). Results Among 401 participants (mean age, 64.9 years ± 8.9 [SD]; 278 male participants), the median onset-to-arterial-puncture time in the EVT group was 402 minutes (IQR, 271-583 minutes). After multivariable adjustment in the IPW-adjusted data, EVT was associated with higher odds of functional independence (odds ratio [OR], 1.55 [95% CI: 1.17, 2.06]) and excellent outcome (OR, 1.48 [95% CI: 1.09, 2.03]) and lower odds of death (OR, 0.65 [95% CI: 0.45, 0.77]) and END (OR, 0.35 [95% CI: 0.20, 0.61]). Subgroup analyses demonstrated EVT-related functional benefit in participants with NIHSS scores of 6-9 but not in those with NIHSS scores of 0-5 (for interaction = .02 for functional independence); however, in participants with NIHSS scores of 0-5, EVT was associated with lower odds of END and death. Sensitivity analyses accounting for treatment crossover showed attenuated functional advantage for EVT. Conclusion In participants with BAO and mild deficits, EVT plus BMM was associated with better outcomes than BMM alone; however, functional benefit was observed in those with NIHSS scores of 6-9 but not those with NIHSS scores of 0-5. title: Stroke and Bleeding Risk in Long-Term Care Residents With Atrial Fibrillation Who Discontinue Anticoagulation.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Atrial fibrillation (AF) leads to more than 100 000 cases of stroke yearly and is particularly prevalent in long-term care (LTC) residents. Anticoagulation (AC) is the mainstay of stroke prevention, but given its risks, clinicians and residents may consider discontinuation at the time of LTC entry. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the association between AC discontinuation and stroke and bleeding risk among LTC residents with AF. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This comparative effectiveness research study with target trial emulation used claims data (2020-2021) from LTC facilities in the US serving Medicare beneficiaries. Medicare beneficiaries with AF receiving AC who entered LTC between April 1 and December 31, 2020, were included; those with additional indications for AC, including prosthetic heart valve or venous thromboembolism, were excluded. Analysis was performed in August 2026. EXPOSURE: Discontinuer vs continuer assignment. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The main outcomes were stroke (including ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attack, and systemic embolism) and bleeding, assessed using Medicare claims. A target trial emulation was conducted with clone censor weighting (CCW) analysis. Specifically, eligible LTC residents were assigned (cloned) to each of 2 strategies: AC discontinuation or AC continuation. Clones were then censored when they deviated from their assigned strategy, and inverse probability of censoring weighting was applied to address informative censoring: residents who deviated differing systematically from those who did not. Subdistribution hazard ratios (sHRs) for stroke and bleeding were then calculated to account for competing mortality and a cause-specific hazard ratio (HR) for death. RESULTS: This study included 15 426 LTC residents (mean [SD] age, 82.6 [7.6] years). Most were female (62.6%). AC discontinuers had 187 strokes, 297 bleeding events, and 3684 deaths over a mean (SD) of 128.9 (177.9) days. AC continuers had 321 strokes, 493 bleeding events, and 5475 deaths over a mean (SD) of 279.6 (204.9) days. Discontinuers had similar stroke risk (sHR, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.93-1.23) and bleeding risk (sHR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.92-1.13) compared with continuers, but discontinuers had higher mortality risk (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.23-1.31). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this target trial emulation with CCW in a cohort of LTC residents with AF, AC discontinuation was not associated with higher stroke or bleeding risk. Very high mortality, unmeasured confounding, and reliance on claims-based outcome ascertainment may have limited the ability to better understand the consequences of AC discontinuation on stroke and bleeding.

OBJECTIVE: To estimate the association between AC discontinuation and stroke and bleeding risk among LTC residents with AF.

title: Trends in Direct Oral Anticoagulant Use for Cancer-Associated Venous Thromboembolism.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) are recommended for selected patients with cancer-associated venous thromboembolism, but their implementation remains heterogeneous. OBJECTIVE: To describe temporal trends in DOAC initiation for cancer-associated venous thromboembolism in France and to identify factors associated with their use. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This nationwide population-based cohort study included adults without recorded contraindications to DOACs and a first treated venous thromboembolism episode between January 1, 2016, and December 31, 2022. Data were collected from the French National Health Data System, a nationwide claims database covering approximately 99% of the population. Analysis was performed from January to August 2025. EXPOSURES: Patients were classified into active cancer and no active cancer groups. Covariates included calendar period, patient characteristics, cancer type and treatment, venous thromboembolism characteristics, and initial prescriber setting. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was DOAC initiation within 30 days after the index venous thromboembolism event. Bayesian structural time series models assessed temporal changes across 2016 to 2018, 2019 to 2020, and 2021 to 2022. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with DOAC initiation among patients with active cancer. RESULTS: Among 683 184 patients with incident treated venous thromboembolism (median [IQR] age, 67 [53-77] years; 347 421 female [51.0%]), 91 954 patients (13.5%) had active cancer while 591 230 (86.5%) had VTE not associated with active cancer. DOAC use increased from 15.3% (95% CI, 15.0%-15.7%) in 2016 to 2018 to 32.6% (95% CI, 32.1%-33.2%) in 2021 to 2022 among patients with active cancer, and from 63.5% (95% CI, 63.3%-63.7%) to 81.1% (95% CI, 80.9%-81.2%) among patients without active cancer. DOAC initiation increased beyond expected secular trends in patients with active cancer, with relative increases of 20.5% (95% credible interval, 13.0%-27.8%) in 2019 to 2020 and 41.3% (95% credible interval, 32.9%-50.2%) in 2021 to 2022. DOAC initiation was less frequent among patients with comorbidities, history of bleeding, gastrointestinal or gynecologic cancer, active brain metastases, or systemic treatment, and when the initial prescriber was a hospital-based physician rather than a general practitioner. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of patients with incident venous thromboembolism, DOAC use increased substantially in patients with active cancer but remained lower than in patients without active cancer and varied across clinical and care-setting characteristics. This lower uptake may reflect both delayed implementation of recent evidence and the need to individualize anticoagulant selection in complex situations.

OBJECTIVE: To describe temporal trends in DOAC initiation for cancer-associated venous thromboembolism in France and to identify factors associated with their use. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This nationwide population-based cohort study included adults without recorded contraindications to DOACs and a first treated venous thromboembolism episode between January 1, 2016, and December 31, 2022.

title: Evaluating the Impact of Therapeutic Anticoagulation Management in Head and Neck Free Tissue Transfer: A Retrospective Study of 126 Cases.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Existing literature on anticoagulation in head and neck free flap reconstruction largely focuses on postoperative thromboprophylaxis. Less is known about preoperative therapeutic anticoagulation, including how perioperative anticoagulation holds, timing of resumption, and anticoagulant class relate to hemorrhagic, thromboembolic, and flap-related complications. This study evaluates these outcomes in anticoagulated patients undergoing head and neck free flap reconstruction and compares complication rates with matched non-anticoagulated controls. METHODS: A retrospective chart review was performed on patients who underwent free flap reconstruction between 2009 and 2023 and had been on therapeutic anticoagulation for over 1 month preoperatively. A matched control group of non-anticoagulated patients was included for comparison. RESULTS: 126 anticoagulated patients (mean age 71.8 years, 75.4% male) were included. The most common indications for anticoagulation were atrial fibrillation (62.7%) and venous thromboembolism (30.2%). Anticoagulation medications included warfarin (49.2%), apixaban (36.5%), rivaroxaban (12.7%), and dabigatran (1.6%). Anticoagulation was stopped an average of 4.4 days preoperatively and resumed 7.8 days postoperatively. Hemorrhagic complications occurred in 14 patients (11.1%), including hematomas and unrelated bleeding. Thromboembolic complications occurred in 9 patients (7.1%), 6 of which resulted in flap failure. On matched cohort analysis, controls had lower odds of any complication (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.21-0.81, p = 0.010), hemorrhagic or thromboembolic complications (OR 0.27, 95% CI 0.11-0.63, p = 0.003), and hemorrhagic complications specifically (OR 0.26, 95% CI 0.09-0.81, p = 0.020), while thromboembolic complication odds were not significantly different between groups (OR 0.47, 95% CI 0.15-1.44, p = 0.19). CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the challenges of managing therapeutic anticoagulation in head and neck free flap surgery, where thromboembolic risk during interruption and hemorrhagic complications upon resumption point to the need for clearer guidelines. Evidence-based protocols are needed to replace discretionary practices and improve outcomes.

This study evaluates these outcomes in anticoagulated patients undergoing head and neck free flap reconstruction and compares complication rates with matched non-anticoagulated controls.

title: Association between admission D-dimer levels and post-stroke epilepsy risk: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-stroke epilepsy (PSE) is a severe complication following acute ischemic stroke (AIS), yet early identification of patients at high risk remains challenging. This study evaluated the association between baseline D-dimer levels and incident PSE within one year after AIS. METHODS: 2 In this secondary analysis of a multicenter retrospective cohort, 21,459 patients with first-ever AIS were included. D-dimer was modeled as a log-transformed continuous variable. Multivariable logistic regression with progressive adjustment, restricted cubic spline analysis, and sensitivity analyses were performed. Internal validation was conducted using bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: The median baseline D-dimer level was 0.92 mg/L (IQR 0.65-1.49). PSE occurred in 936 patients (4.36%). After full adjustment, each doubling of D-dimer was associated with a 3.3-fold increase in PSE odds (OR 3.33, 95% CI 2.94-3.78). The association remained consistent in sensitivity analyses excluding patients with deep vein thrombosis (OR 3.86, 95% CI 3.37-4.43), atrial fibrillation (OR 3.50, 95% CI 3.04-4.04), or extreme D-dimer values (OR 3.41, 95% CI 2.99-3.91). A non-linear relationship was observed, with PSE risk rising more steeply at higher D-dimer levels. The C-statistic for the fully adjusted model was 0.968. CONCLUSION: Elevated baseline D-dimer levels were independently associated with an increased risk of PSE within one year after AIS. As a routinely available biomarker, D-dimer may inform risk assessment in acute stroke units; however, external validation in independent cohorts with prospective PSE ascertainment is required before clinical implementation.

title: Short-Term Outcomes of Lower-Extremity Surgical Revascularization for Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia Among Yemeni Patients: A Prospective Observational Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) carries a high risk of amputation and mortality. We evaluated short-term clinical, hemodynamic, and quality-of-life outcomes after open lower-extremity surgical revascularization in a Yemeni cohort. METHODS: This single-center prospective observational cohort study was conducted at Al-Thawra Modern General Hospital, Sana'a, Yemen. We enrolled 39 consecutive adults with CLTI (Rutherford categories 4-6) who were selected for and considered fit to undergo open lower-extremity surgical revascularization between December 2022 and September 2024; follow-up was completed in December 2024. The study protocol was reviewed and approved by the Al-Thawra Hospital Ethics Committee (approval no. 33-2026), and written informed consent was obtained from all participants. The study was not registered. This was an exploratory consecutive cohort; no formal sample-size calculation was performed, and no contemporaneous endovascular, nonoperative, or primary-amputation comparator group was included. Primary endpoints were graft patency and limb salvage at three months. Secondary outcomes were secondary patency, postoperative complications, and changes in ankle-brachial index (ABI) and Vascular Quality of Life Questionnaire-6 (VascuQoL-6) scores. Paired comparisons used Wilcoxon signed-rank tests; Fisher's exact tests were used for categorical comparisons. RESULTS: The mean age was 60.9 years (SD 9.7), and 30 patients (76.9%) were male. Diabetes mellitus and hypertension were present in 34 (87.2%) and 30 (76.9%) patients, respectively. Nineteen patients (48.7%) had ischemic rest pain, and 20 (51.3%) had tissue loss. Great saphenous vein (GSV) and polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) grafts were used in 28 (71.8%) and 11 (28.2%) patients, respectively. At three months, primary patency was 84.6% (33/39 grafts; 95% CI 70.3%-92.8%), secondary patency was 89.7% (35/39 grafts; 95% CI 76.4%-95.9%), and limb salvage was 89.7% (35/39 patients; 95% CI 76.4%-95.9%). Given the small cohort, the confidence intervals around these estimates were relatively wide. Among the 35 patients with limb preservation, mean ABI increased from 0.35 (SD 0.11) to 0.55 (SD 0.12; mean difference 0.21, 95% CI 0.19-0.23; p<0.001), and mean VascuQoL-6 score increased from 10.3 (SD 2.9) to 16.6 (SD 4.0; mean difference 6.3, 95% CI 5.6-7.1; p<0.001). Complications occurred in nine patients (23.1%). In an exploratory unadjusted subgroup analysis, GSV use was associated with higher primary patency than PTFE use (92.9% vs 63.6%, p=0.042). CONCLUSION: In this single-center prospective cohort, open surgical revascularization was feasible and was associated with 89.7% limb salvage and 84.6% primary patency at three months. Improvements in ABI and VascuQoL-6 were observed among patients with limb preservation. Autologous GSV use was associated with higher primary patency; this finding requires confirmation in larger, adjusted studies.

We evaluated short-term clinical, hemodynamic, and quality-of-life outcomes after open lower-extremity surgical revascularization in a Yemeni cohort. METHODS: This single-center prospective observational cohort study was conducted at Al-Thawra Modern General Hospital, Sana'a, Yemen.

title: Transcatheter Electrosurgical Aortic Septotomy Across the Spectrum of Type B Aortic Dissection: Feasibility, Technical Lessons, and Bailout Strategies.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter electrosurgical aortic septotomy (TEAS) has been introduced to optimise luminal geometry during endovascular repair of complex type B aortic dissection (TBAD), but data across dissection phases and on complication management remain limited. This study reports early outcomes, quantitative common lumen creation, and bailout strategies from a consecutive single centre experience. METHOD: Eight consecutive patients underwent TEAS, between December 2024 and January 2026, as an adjunct to thoracic endovascular aortic repair or physician modified fenestrated endograft for acute, subacute, or chronic TBAD, including post-type A repair and genetic aortopathy. Pre-procedural and follow up computed tomography angiography (CTA) quantified true lumen and common lumen cross sectional area. Septotomy technical success, peri-operative outcomes, complications, and early follow up were assessed. RESULTS: 2 2 The mean age was 51.1 ± 17 years; five were men. Two patients were acute, two subacute, and four chronic; two had Marfan syndrome, both redo cases after previous open repair. Septotomy technical success was 100%. The median cross sectional area increased from 174.5 mm(pre-procedural true lumen) to 1 007 mm(follow up CTA common lumen) after TEAS (5.3 fold increase). There were no 30 day, in hospital, or aortic related deaths. Three major procedure related complications (38%) occurred, all in non-acute cases and all managed endovascularly: one iliac lamellar dislodgement requiring kissing stents, one external iliac rupture treated with stent grafting, and one delayed superior mesenteric artery occlusion managed with stenting. All acute cases were uneventful. Median clinical follow up was 32 days (range 22 - 308) and median imaging follow up was 20 days (range 2 - 265), with no late deaths, no aortic re-interventions, and no aneurysmal dilatation of the non-stented TEAS treated segment. CONCLUSION: TEAS may be considered across acute, subacute, and chronic TBAD, including redo and connective tissue disease cases, enabling reproducible common lumen creation and landing zone optimisation. All complications were recognised and managed endovascularly and were observed only in non-acute dissections, although the sample size precluded meaningful assessment of any relationship between dissection phase and technical risk. These findings support TEAS as a feasible adjunct in carefully selected complex dissections, offer practical principles for safe adoption, and reflect an early experience that may be influenced by the learning curve of this technically demanding procedure.

title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Analyses Identify CCR2-Dependent Monocyte-Smooth Muscle Cell Crosstalk in Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Aortic aneurysm (AA) involves inflammatory recruitment and vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) remodeling, but the cellular contribution of candidate chemokine receptors remains unclear. We prioritized reproducible AA-associated genes, localized their cellular sources, and tested whether monocyte CCR2 influences human aortic smooth muscle cells (HASMCs). METHODS: Differentially expressed genes shared by GSE57691 and GSE7084 underwent enrichment, protein-protein interaction, regulatory-network, and drug-gene analyses. Hub genes were assessed in GSE9106 and localized in GSE166676 single-cell RNA-sequencing data. CCR2-silenced THP-1 monocytic cells were indirectly co-cultured with HASMCs. CCR2 knockdown was verified by quantitative PCR; HASMC remodeling-related proteins and 24-h scratch-wound closure were evaluated. RESULTS: p p p We identified 107 common upregulated genes and ten immune-related hubs. CCR2 was monocyte-enriched and higher in AA cells overall (= 0.00799) and AA monocytes (= 0.00440). THP-1 co-culture increased COL3A1 and SPP1, decreased α-SMA and TPM, and increased HASMC wound closure. CCR2 silencing partially reversed these changes and decreased wound closure versus siNC-THP-1 cells (< 0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Multi-omic evidence and non-contact co-culture support CCR2-dependent monocyte-HASMC paracrine crosstalk in AA-associated remodeling. The responsible mediators and in vivo relevance require further study.
